articleTitle: Efficient Energy Routing in Smart Grid Networks Using Fractional Knapsack and Dijkstra Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Smart Grids (SG) have opened up new avenues for research, particularly in the field of energy routing. However, energy routing poses several challenges such as identifying the most efficient routes and selecting the optimal group of producers to purchase from. Although heuristic methods are currently used to address these challenges, they often fall short of delivering optimal solutions. In this paper, we propose to address both the subset selection problem and the efficient path problem in a small residential area using a greedy method. Our approach formulates the problem as a fractional knapsack problem, with the objective of maximizing energy value while considering capacity constraints. To determine the optimal routes based on their distance, we employ the Dijkstra algorithm. We then use the proposed greedy function to determine the optimal set of sellers for every consumer. Based on the simulation results, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Monitoring System Using Android-Based Mobile Application with Cloud Firebase
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the major causes of death around the world. Continuous surveillance of cardiovascular patients becomes necessary to monitor their heart status outside the hospital by mainly checking their electrocardiogram (ECG) signal. In this paper, we conceived a cardiovascular monitoring system using an Android-based mobile application with Cloud Firebase. The present system is dedicated to remotely monitor cardiovascular patients' hearts and present a decision aid tool to help the physicians to take the appropriate medical actions in case of an abnormal heartbeat. The hardware part of the system communicates with the designed Android-based application, named Healthy, by using the Bluetooth technology. It continuously acquires the ECG data, measures the current patient's heartbeat, send them in real-time and display them on the mobile application. In addition, the Healthy application notifies the attending doctor in the Google Firebase-Cloud in case an abnormal heartbeat occurs. Consequently, the patient would receive an alarm notification on his Smartphone. The conducted experimental results confirmed that the hardware ECG monitoring device works efficiently. In addition, our developed Healthy application is easy to use and flexible for the users. Finally, we simulated an abnormal heartbeat by disconnecting an electrode. The Healthy application sent the corresponding heartbeat to the Cloud and notified both the test subject and the doctor about the abnormal heartbeat.

articleTitle: Artificial Search Algorithm for Parameters Optimization of Li-Ion Battery Electrical Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Leveraging AI (Artificial Intelligence) for parameter identification in battery models aids in making informed decisions about battery design, efficiency, and performance, which is crucial for electric vehicles and renewable energy systems. This article proposes the use of the Adolescent Identity Search Algorithm (AISA) to estimate parameters of the third-order Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) for Li-ion battery. AISA introduces an innovative metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the process of adolescent identity formation. This novel AISA-driven method achieves high accuracy with a low computational cost, making it suitable for real-world applications. The resulting RMSE of 8.50988265e-03 obtained in this study demonstrates the efficiency of the introduced approach for battery modeling and its potential for practical use in intelligent systems and sustainable applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of the prediction performance of decision tree-based algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Due to their many benefits, decision trees are extensively utilized to solve a variety of classification problems in the real world. Consequently, creating efficient and effective decision trees remains a common challenge for researchers in the fields of machine learning and data mining. In the literature, various decision tree algorithms with different attribute selection criteria are introduced. Although the currently available decision tree algorithms achieve different performances, none of them can produce optimal decision trees for a range of data sets. In this study, the efficacy of two traditional decision tree techniques is contrasted with the efficacy of two more recent decision tree approaches. On eleven real-world data sets, the four methods are compared in terms of four evaluation metrics: classification accuracy, tree depth, leaf nodes, and tree construction time.

articleTitle: Integrating Ontology and Machine Learning for Enhanced Decision Support in Thyroid Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In recent years, decision support systems have emerged as valuable tools in the field of medical diagnosis and prediction. With the increasing prevalence of thyroid diseases, accurate and timely prediction plays a crucial role in improving patient outcomes. However, the adoption of traditional black-box machine learning models for thyroid disease prediction is hindered by their lack of interpretability, making it challenging for clinicians to trust and understand the decision-making process. Our innovative approach combines machine learning, specifically decision trees, with ontology integration for interpretability. The ontology classifier provides insights into the model's decision-making process. The dataset used comprises 9172 observations, each represented by 31 features, accessible for download on Kaggle. According to the results The ontology model surpassed Decision tree model.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Predicting Personality Traits from Eye Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Recently, personality prediction holds significant importance in human centered systems, particularly in decision support systems, the smart industry, and the development of human machine interfaces. Eyes can reveal deep insights into a person's personality, so people's visual behavior could better reflect their personality. In this research, we demonstrate that machine learning techniques can predict individual personality traits from eye movements and minimize biases and errors reported by self-reported questionnaires. We performed an experiment using Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithms to predict individuals' Big Five personality traits based on their visual behavior. The findings of this study demonstrate that the proposed methodology outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Mobile Application as a Learning Material in Ecotourism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Mobile games play significant roles in today's education. The teaching and learning process becomes more active and attractive by using mobile games. EcoMode application is created for Fostering Eco – Innovative Business Model Development in SMEs in Hospitality Industry and offers three different study models. The EcoMode application focuses on giving theoretical knowledge to beginners in ecotourism. It is based on the best practice of EU countries and consists of three different examination models. This study emphasizes trainers who are likely to use today's technology in ecotourism education. This study designed and developed an EcoMode application that allowed trainers to use mobile technology in ecotourism.

articleTitle: Alzheimer Disease Detection Using Advanced Transfer Learning Techniques on MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurological disorder that has a profound impact on millions of individuals globally. It is imperative to identify and diagnose AD at an early stage with precision, as this plays a crucial role in timely intervention and effective treatment. In recent years, the utilization of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in conjunction with deep learning has demonstrated promising results for assisting in the detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This study introduces a methodology for detecting AD by employing MRI images and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Five pre-trained CNN models, including MobileNetV2, ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, InceptionV3, and DenseNet-201, are employed for the transfer learning (TL) task. A comparative study and detailed analysis of the performances achieved by each model are presented. The models are trained on a large dataset of MRI images, consisting of both healthy and AD-affected brains with hyper-parameters tuning. During training, the CNNs learn to automatically identify patterns and discriminative features that differentiate between normal and AD-affected brain regions. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a comprehensive set of experiments is conducted using publicly available datasets. From the experimental study, it is observed that the TL approach using the five pretrained CNN models achieves good performances in the two class classification problem of Very Mild Demented and Non Demented individuals. The results of this paper contribute to the growing field of computer-aided diagnosis for AD and emphasize the effectiveness of deep learning techniques, particularly CNNs, in the analysis of medical imaging data.

articleTitle: Physical and System Level Power Reduction Technique for NoC Architectures: Overview of State of the Art
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Power dissipation and energy consumption are key factors for the performance improvement of modern technology systems. In recent years, several strategies have been proposed to solve the power management issues on embedded systems. In this paper, we classify the state of the art of those techniques. Classification is done based on run-time, activation, and idle state of the different components of the network on chip (NoC). We illustrate the requirement of power management based on several important parameters. A highlight is put on the drawbacks and benefits. Also, classification is done based on different NoC abstraction levels. However, by this paper, we intend to guide the researchers and application developers in getting insights about the strategies of power management techniques that will lead to the design of more efficient high performances in embedded systems of the future.

articleTitle: Plant Leaf Disease Prediction and Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: One of the primary causes of decreased agricultural production in terms of both quality and quantity is the prevalence of plant diseases. Plant diseases continuously emerge on plant leaves due to ongoing changes in plant structure and cultivation methods. Initially, these diseases affect the leaves and subsequently spread throughout the entire plant, resulting in a significant impact on the variety and yield of crops that can be grown. Therefore, effective control of infection spread and promotion of robust plant growth relies on accurate classification and early detection of plant leaf diseases. In this study, a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) model is proposed for the classification of plant diseases, aiming to address these challenges. The model utilizes the PlantVillage dataset, which consists of images showcasing 14 different healthy and diseased crop leaves, categorized into 38 distinct classes. Experimental results demonstrate that the CNN model achieves a training accuracy of 98.01 % and a test accuracy of 94.33%. These findings highlight that the model offers a highly effective solution for the early diagnosis of leaf diseases.

articleTitle: Enhancing Decision Making with Semantic-Based Hybrid Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Decision making can be a complex and challenging task, particularly in the context of an overwhelming amount of information available on the web. Recommender systems have emerged as a solution to aid decision making by suggesting relevant items based on users' preferences and needs. However, traditional content-based recommender systems have been criticized for their lack of diversity in recommendations. On the other hand, collaborative filtering suffers from scalability issues due to the high computational complexity of similarity calculations for large datasets. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid recommender system that leverages Linked Open Data and Ant Colony Optimization. Our approach utilizes semantic databases to improve the precision of recommendations and ACO algorithm to optimize the selection of diverse items. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed system outperforms traditional recommendation systems in terms of decision aid and provides users with personalized and diverse recommendations. This research can contribute to the development of decision aid applications and improve the quality of decision making.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dermoscopy-Based Skin Lesions Diagnosis: A Fusion of Convolutional Neural Networks and Self-Training
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Automatic classification of skin lesions from der-moscopic images is a challenging task due to the similarities in visual features across different lesion types, such as size, shape, texture, and colour. Additional challenges include the presence of artefacts, limited data availability, and overfitting issues associated with deep learning architectures. This research aims to address these challenges by proposing a computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system that accurately classifies skin lesions using both a publicly available ISIC 2019 challenge dataset and a private dataset. The study introduces three main tasks to achieve this objective. Task 1 focuses on improving data quality by addressing imbalanced class distribution, missing values, and der-moscopic multi-resolutions. Task 2 involves developing the CAD system using transfer learning with a pretrained Noisy Student (EfficientNet-L2) architecture, incorporating additional metadata through a dense neural network concatenated with the CNN output. The classifier, consisting of eight units representing skin lesion classes and an unknown class, follows. The proposed NS-EfficientN et- L2 model effectively classifies skin lesions, surpassing state-of-the-art methods, including the winner of the ISIC 2019 challenge for skin lesion classification. This research provides a promising approach for accurately diagnosing skin lesions based on dermoscopic Images.

Index Terms: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

articleTitle: Algerian Electricity Consumption Forecasting with Artificial Neural Networks Using a Multiple Seasonal-Trend Decomposition Using LOESS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Electricity consumption plays a vital role in the development and sustainability of a nation. This paper focuses on the analysis of electricity consumption in Algeria and the use of the MSTL (Multiple Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS) method to build load forecasting short term models. The MSTL method, a variant of the classic decomposition method, offers a powerful tool for analyzing time series with multiple seasons. By breaking down the time series into seasonal, trend, and residual components, MSTL can identify underlying patterns and make accurate predictions. Using the MSTL method, the load is decomposed into several components, Trend, Seasonlity and Residual component where the latter carries the high frequency load changes. Artificial Neural network of LSTM and classical MLP types are then developed to model and predict the residual part. The complete load forecasting is then obtained, adding the subsequent components.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Dead Time Performance in Single-Phase Inverter MOSFETs and IGBTs Under Varying Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In power electronic converters, the dead time of a transistor plays a critical role in determining its overall performance and efficiency. In this paper, experimental tests were conducted on MOSFETs and IGBTs, both of which are important components in power electronics, to assess their dead time performance under varying loads for a single leg of a three-phase inverter application. While controlling the low side of the MOSFET or IGBT is relatively straightforward, optimizing the dead time control for high side voltage can be challenging. To tackle this challenge, a three-phase inverter leg and test bench were set up for both MOSFETs and IGBTs. The gate drive and optocoupler were utilized to enable the controller to receive inverse signals. Subsequently, multiple tests were performed under various conditions to evaluate the performance of the transistors dead time. The experimental results demonstrate the crucial role of load in achieving optimized dead time in various applications. By shedding light on the impact of load on dead time, valuable insights are provided into improving the performance and efficiency of power electronic converters.

articleTitle: The Effect of Source Data on Graphical Pentagons DGA Methods for Detecting Incipient Faults in Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Detecting power transformer faults at an early stage is crucial for ensuring the safety and uninterrupted operation of electrical systems. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) serves as a valuable strategy for diagnosing faults in oil-filled transformers. Oil plays a vital role in transformer operation, serving as both a cooling and insulation medium. It also acts as an indicator for assessing thermal and electrical stresses within the transformer by analyzing the composition of dissolved gases in the oil. In this paper, the graphical techniques of the Pentagons for each of Duval Pentagon method and Mansour Pentagon method were discussed at different data sources. The dataset comprises 357 samples, with 117 samples sourced from IEC TC 10 data and 240 samples obtained from Egyptian laboratories. The Duval Pentagon method demonstrates superior performance, achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 69.23% when applied to the IEC TC 10 data. Conversely, the Mansour Pentagon method outperforms the Duval Pentagon method with a diagnostic accuracy of 68.75% when applied to the Egyptian laboratory data. This paper is a proposal to find a new graphical method that adapts to the variables of the source data. The proposed approach aims to address the challenges posed by diverse data sources and provide a more comprehensive and adaptable framework for transformer fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Computer Vision Techniques for Intelligent Detection and Classification of Waste Sorting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the application of computer vision techniques in waste classification and sorting within the context of Industry 4.0. The Fourth Industrial Revolution has revolutionized manufacturing and industrial processes through advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and automation. Computer vision, coupled with machine learning algorithms, has emerged as a critical enabler, offering transformative solutions for various industrial applications. In this study, we explore the potential of computer vision techniques as a user-friendly tool for improving waste management practices. By leveraging advanced algorithms and neural networks, we develop a waste classification model capable of automating the identification and sorting of waste materials. The model is trained using a diverse dataset of waste material images and refined through an iterative process. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the trained model in accurately classifying and sorting waste items. This research contributes to the optimization of waste management processes within the industry 4.0 framework, driving advancements towards efficient and sustainable waste management practices.

articleTitle: Requests Satisfaction in a Virtual Web Services System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper defines analytical models for a Web services system, with two stations on tandem queue, for evaluating the request satisfaction involving two exponential servers, each having its own waiting queue. The first waiting queue is unlimited. The arrivals of requests follow a Poisson process, and after service completion, they can either leave the system or join the second line. The obtained model has not a product form; and the only way to obtain its performances is by computing its steady-state probabilities. To this end, we must use balance equations that give us unlimited equations with unlimited unknowns. In this case the only solution is the use of approximation methods. In this paper we use the truncation method to approximate the performances of our model with the performances of a truncated model. We also use the strong stability method to estimate the error of this approximation. Furthermore, we compute the system's response time, and the average number of clients in the system in terms of the arrival rate of clients requests.

articleTitle: A Decision Model for Talent Management in the Indian Fintech Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The fintech industry in India has experienced exceptional growth, but talent management challenges pose major roadblocks to its longevity. India's fintech industry can maximize its potential, nurture innovation, and establish itself as a global fintech powerhouse if it addresses the skills gap through an effective talent management framework. The purpose of this study was to explore the difficulties HR managers confronted concerning talent management using a structured interviewing method and purposive sampling. This paper seeks to provide insights and recommendations that will enable fintech firms to navigate talent management challenges, attract skilled professionals, and foster a thriving fintech ecosystem in the country.

articleTitle: Classical Machine Learning and Transformer Models for Offensive and Abusive Language Classification on Dziri Language
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Offensive and abusive language identification is a challenging task, especially for low-resource languages such as Dziri, a dialect of Algerian Arabic. In this paper, we propose two approaches to enhance the performance of this task for Dziri. The first approach fine-tunes several pre-trained transformer models, including DziriBERT (a BERT-based model trained on Dziri corpus), AraBERT (a BERT-based model trained on Arabic corpus), BERT-base model (a BERT-based model trained on English corpus), and XLM-Roberta (a multilingual BERT-based model trained on 100 languages). The second approach applies a tailored preprocessing pipeline for the Dziri dialect, optimized chi-2 feature selection, and optimized SVM hyper-parameters using the Bayesian optimization. The evaluation demonstrates that our approach substantially improves the identification score compared to baseline classifiers. However, DziriBERT still outperforms our approaches by 5.83 % and 1.17 % of F -score in binary and ternary classification, respectively. The code to reproduce the results is available at: https://github.com/Bouchenemehdi24/Off-Abus-Dziri.

articleTitle: Effect of Barbiturate Coma Therapy on Patients with Resistant Intracranial Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Increased intracranial pressure (ICP) after traumatic brain injury can lead to death of patients. This work aimed to evaluate the impact of barbiturate coma therapy (BCT) on intractable intracranial hypertension patients. We conducted a statistical analysis of studies published up to May 2023. The model showed a positive effect of BCT during treatment., the ICP in the experimental group of patients was 11.29 mmHg lower (on average) than in the control group (mean difference with 95% confidence interval is −11.29 [−16.19., −6.39], <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}-\text{value} < 0.00001$</tex>). The model also showed a positive effect of BCT on the patient's neurological condition (MD with a 95% CI is 0.73 [0.37., 1.10], <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}-\text{value} < 0.0001$</tex>). BCT significantly reduces intracranial pressure and improves the patient's neurological condition. Although our results are statistically significant, they are based on limited data from four clinical trials. Future studies may evaluate the possible side effects of BCT.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Bioimpedance Measurement System Based on AD5933 Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we address the critical need for a low and stable impedance at the skin-electrode interface to ensure precise and dependable biosignal acquisition. Regarding this matter an impedance analyzer is a necessary equipment in the laboratory but due to its higher cost, it is not available in the majority of them. Our study introduces a cost-effective impedance measurement system utilizing EVAL-AD5933EBZ, enhanced with an analog front-end circuit design, and employs a four-electrode strategy measurement method. The primary objective is to investigate the behavior of complex skin-electrode impedance and assess its stability over time for dry and commercial gel electrodes in order to evaluate the developed design. Our experimental tests were conducted within the frequency range of 5 kHz to 50 kHz. The results validate the accurate performance of our measurement system and demonstrate that the studied dry electrodes exhibited a similar behavior to the commercial electrode. These findings provide valuable insights into the impedance characteristics of the skin-electrode interface.

articleTitle: Use of Impedance and Phase Measurements to Define Thresholds of Power Transformers Insulating Mineral Oil Capability When Subjected to Successive Discharges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Power transformers represent the most expensive and vital equipments in power distribution and transmission networks. Their real time diagnosis is of great importance in order to ensure them a safe and permanent operating. The performance and reliability of these equipments is directly dependent on the electrical discharges activity that could occur inside the mineral oil that is filled inside them as an insulation and cooling fluid. This paper discusses the effect of applying simultaneous electrical discharges of low energy under AC voltage on the characteristics of the impedance and phase of the insulating mineral oil with frequency ranging from 20 Hz to 10 MHz. The impedance and phase of the oil are measured with a high precision LCR-meter in a point-plane electrode system and a gap of 2.5 mm. The performed measurements provide a well correlation with the degree of degradation of the mineral oil and hence with its capacity and resistivity when submitted to AC high voltage discharges. Threshold values can be defined to judge whether the transformer must be stopped and repaired.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Route Simulation: A Preliminary Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This article presents a NetLogo-based multi-agent simulator developed to optimize route and task planning using electric vehicles for travel between branches of Société Générale. The simulator takes into account constraints linked to the limited autonomy of electric vehicle batteries in the dense urban context of branches. We carried out simulation tests to evaluate the simulator's performance and generate optimized routes, minimizing distances travelled and CO2 emissions. This simulator represents a promising first step in the search for innovative solutions for planning electric vehicle routes between branches.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Supply Chain in Algeria: Enhancing Transparency and Security of Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This article specializes in the implementation of Blockchain generation in deliver chain control in Algeria, with the aim of improving transparency and security of operations. The article highlights the importance of supply chains for local businesses and the global economy, introducing the decentralized architecture and secure capabilities of blockchain's distributed ledger. The work implements blockchain technology in supply chain management in Algeria, with a view to improving transparency and security of operations. We begin by highlighting the importance of blockchain as a key business priority and its potential to reshape the future of business through the process of reform and reconstruction. Next, we present an extensive overview of the advantages and limitations of blockchain technology. By analyzing its advantages and disadvantages, we also look at existing solutions to address these drawbacks. Finally, a use case is presented to validate this technology in the pharmaceutical sector in Algeria.

articleTitle: Implementation of ANP-TOPSIS for Prioritizing Switching Device Placement (Case Study: Rantau Prapat Distribution Network)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Continuing from our previous research, this study further examines the operations of PLN UP3 Rantau Prapat, the state-owned electricity company responsible for four regencies in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, with a particular focus on the installation of load break switches (LBS) within the distribution network to enhance operational reliability. Shifting from the FAHP-TOPSIS methodology to the ANP-TOPSIS approach, it investigates ten LBS units across 30 designated feeders. The criteria used for evaluation remain consistent with prior research, encompassing Energy Not Served (ENS), System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), feeder length, network availability, and feeder load. This transition introduces a new evaluation perspective, comparing variations and altered criterion weights via the ANP approach to influence the resulting TOPSIS rankings. In conclusion, this study finds that the application of the ANP-TOPSIS methodology to the evaluation of LBS placement in the distribution network demonstrates minimal changes in criterion weights, which are not statistically significant. These changes have a negligible impact on the rankings of alternatives and do not lead to significant alterations in the allocation of LBS units. Notably, ULP Aek Kanopan receives the highest allocation of LBS units, with a total of three units.

articleTitle: The Theoretical Modeling of Financial Performance of Insurance Companies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Given the crucial role that financial performance plays in guiding the decision-making process for investors, shareholders, regulators, and corporate leaders, this article presents a theoretical model for assessing the financial performance of insurance companies, specifically focusing on identifying the determinants of financial performance within the insurance sector and their corresponding variables.

articleTitle: Study and Implementation on FPGA of Human Recognition System via Iris Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Due to the distinct and consistent traits found in the human iris, iris recognition systems have garnered significant attention for biometric identification and authentication purposes. The project presents an extensive investigation and practical implementation of an iris recognition system on an Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA). The primary objective is to develop an efficient and dependable biometric authentication solution. The study introduces an innovative software-based approach that improves system performance and addresses critical challenges associated with iris recognition technology. The valuable insights obtained from this project are expected to drive future advancements in iris recognition technology, while also contributing to the ongoing development of more secure and trustworthy biometric authentication systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing hyperparameters of linear SVM classifiers using the support method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The support vector machine (SVM) is a popular classifier known for its powerful generalization capabilities and its wide application in a variety of fields. In order to achieve optimal performance of this model, the user is required to provide values for the tuning parameters: the regularization cost parameter and kernel parameters. In this work, we focus on the optimization of the regularization parameter, by developing a new algorithm based on the direct support method that allows for computing all breakpoints that minimize the number of misclassified examples and maximize the margin. This approach is iterative and formed by two phases. Phase 1 is used to calculate the first optimal solution corresponding to the initial value of the regularization parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> = 1/C, while phase 2 is used to iteratively calculate the rest of the breakpoints.

articleTitle: Lax-net: Freezing of Gait Detection in Parkinson's Disease Using LSTM with Attention and XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder marked by motor symptoms like gait freezing (FoG), which notably affects patients' mobility and overall quality of life. Early detection of FOG episodes is crucial for timely intervention and reducing the risk of falls and injuries. In this paper, we present Lax-net, a deep learning-based approach for the early detection of FOG using wearable sensor data with time series information. These data often exhibit complex temporal dependencies, making it challenging to extract meaningful features and accurately classify them. To address this challenge, our proposed method combines the strengths of LSTM with attention mechanisms to capture temporal relationships and identify important features in the data. The derived features are then fed into the XGBoost model, a robust classifier with the ability to grasp non-linear relationships. We evaluate the performance of our proposed method on a benchmark dataset, comparing it with other state-of-the-art methods. The results demonstrate that our combined approach achieves superior accuracy and outperforms individual models such as LSTM and XGBoost.

articleTitle: Evaluation of reduction system of gas flaring and venting and petroleum production optimization Case: Unit of GCR-GEA-SONATRACH
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In recent years, Algeria has experienced a growing demand for hydrocarbons on the world and national market, in return production has fallen considerably according to figures recently published by the National Statistics Office (NSO). In the face of this crucial situation, in particular competition, decision-makers are called upon to be reactive to this production problem, Techniques such as compression and gas reinjection, which aims to optimize production and reduce the volume of flared gas and associated gas loss, are installed to ensure the sustainability of these industries. The realization of this technique is a systematic solution to both production and environmental problems; hence the interest to ensure the safe operation of these systems. In this context, our contribution aims; the analysis of the malfunctions of the “GAZ LIFT” compression and reinjection unit; by the development of a methodological approach based on operational safety tools in order to provide management decision-makers with a decision-making tool relating to measures to control these malfunctions and therefore ensure the optimization of production, the valorization of natural resources, and the protection of the environment. Finally, the purpose of this article is to demonstrate the contribution of methods and tools of operational safety to the dimensions of sustainable, economic, environmental and social development.

articleTitle: Reducing Food Waste in Poultry Cold Chain: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Food loss is one of the challenges in Cold Chain (CC), which can lead to serious problems with human safety, environment, and economies around the world. Recently, reducing food loss has drawn public attention; previous studies mostly gave attention to food loss drivers in the retailer-consumer stages of the supply chain. In this study we focused on identifying Food-Loss-Factors (FLF) all over the CC, and developed an approach based on multi criteria decision making methods and fuzzy sets to rank FLF according to their influence on food loss in poultry sector. The first phase concerns the identification of FLFs based on the literature as well as experts opinions in the poultry field. To ensure robust results, the fuzzy Delphi method is utilized to achieve a consistency level greater than 75% among all group members. In the second phase, fuzzy AHP method is applied to weigh the FLFs and rank them accordingly. The outcomes of this research offer decision-makers in the CC sector a valuable guide to formulating efficient strategies aimed at reducing food loss during logistic activities.

articleTitle: Hub Location Problems: Classification and Bibliometric Analysis of Relevant Works
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed study of the well-known hub location problem (HLP). Its primary objective is to introduce novice readers to the complexity of this field. We focus on a review of pioneering work in HLP and have classified it according to several criteria. To do this, several classes have been identified, in particular: single and multiple allocation, full and partial hub network and capacitated hub location problem. Finally, a bibliometric study is provided to highlight the progress of research in the field of HLPs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Data Transmission in IoT-Based Drone Networks Through Fog Area Division
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with cameras, sensors, and GPS receivers generate a significant amount of data that is transmitted to a base station in an Internet of Things (IoT) environment. This paper addresses the issue of repeated data transmission from drones to a base station in IoT-based networks, leading to redundancy and inefficiencies. The challenges include limited bandwidth, network congestion, and increased costs. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel solution that involves dividing the fog area into smaller parts and optimizing data distribution among drones. We introduce the concepts of fog area division, data distribution factors, and shot-by-shot capture approach. By implementing these techniques, we aim to minimize redundancy, optimize bandwidth utilization, reduce network congestion, and lower costs in IoT-based drone networks.

articleTitle: The Impact of E-Money Multiplier on Economic Growth in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the impact of the e-money multiplier on Indonesian economic growth. The quarterly data used are sourced from Central Bank of Indonesia's publications from 2013Q1 to 2022Q4. The collected data are analyzed using the Error Correction Model (ECM) method because the data of all variables are stationary at the same I(1) level. The results show that the e-money multiplier tends to increase the money supply in the long run. Economic growth has been boosted by the money supply which is influenced by the e-money multiplier in the short term. This study also found that sustainable growth, which continues to increase both in the short and long term, is controlled by two main factors. These are the large amount of money supply in society and high transaction activity using money, also known as high money velocity. Because the e-money multiplier turns out to have a good impact on economic growth, it is expected that Central Bank of Indonesia keeps to monitor changes in the money supply due to the existence of electronic money. That situation may turn out to be detrimental to economic growth if the desire of the community to transact is weak.

articleTitle: Investigate the impact of the probability of rupture on the Weibull parameters of gray cast iron through calculated expressions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This research focuses on the tensile behavior of gray cast iron samples containing a high percentage of carbon with spheroidal graphite, specifically for EN-GJS-500-7 key rings. An empirical model is applied to address various issues, and in the case of our gray cast iron with a high carbon content and spheroidal graphite, each link represents a volume element. The weakest links correspond to the volume elements that contain the most critical defects. Through experimental testing, the specimens were subjected to rupture, resulting in different rupture stresses, denoted as σ1 and σ6. These rupture stresses are associated with a probability level of rupture based on their rank, denoted as i. To calculate the probability of rupture, three analytic expressions are utilized: Pr = i / (N + 1), Pr = (i-0.3) / (i + 0.4), and Pr = (i-O.S) / N. These expressions allow for the estimation of the probability of rupture for each rank i. The fragility of the material's failure is evident from the low measured values of the Weibull modulus. Furthermore, an analysis of the load-displacement curves enables the quantification of the material's resistance to crack propagation. By examining these curves, the main mechanisms governing the failure of the material can be preliminarily investigated.

articleTitle: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Optimization Techniques for Efficient Delivery
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The rise of e-commerce and its significant impact on transport and logistics have prompted companies to question the efficiency of parcel deliveries. The question of parcel delivery efficiency comes up against a well-known classic problem in logistics, namely the vehicle routing problem (VRP), which consists in optimizing vehicle route predictions in order to save time while maximizing delivered customer satisfaction. This is the objective of this article, which proposes to combine machine learning techniques linked to artificial intelligence, such as K-Means, DBSCAN and OPTICS, to group delivery points into clusters, thus reducing the complexity of the problem. Building on these clustering methods, our paper highlights the use of the Tabu search algorithm to optimize delivery rounds within each cluster. By exploring different optimization approaches, we plan to deploy the Tabu search algorithm on several clusters while adding a constraint on the number of deliveries per round, which will result in more efficient delivery round solutions tailored to our operational constraints. Using this combined approach, our paper proposes practical recommendations to help decision-makers improve their delivery service and respond effectively to the logistical challenges of the e-commerce sector.

articleTitle: Deep Classifier Fusion-based Multi-Classification of Chest X-rays for COVID-19 Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In the last three years, The COVID-19 pandemic has placed immense strain on healthcare systems worldwide. Imaging techniques, such as Chest X-Ray (CXR) images, play an essential role in diagnosing COVID-19. Recently, Computer Aided Diagnosis systems based on Deep Learning have been widely used to identify COVID-19 from other upper respiratory diseases such as viral pneumonia. To enhance COVID-19 diagnosis using CXR images, this article proposes a methodology that combines three deep learning models renowned for their depth and feature extraction capabilities: ResNet, DenseNet, and VGG. The model’ strengths are harnessed using Aggregation techniques such as stacking and voting (majority, weighted, average), to improve prediction accuracy. Moreover, the used dataset was subjected to preprocessing, balancing, and augmentation techniques, including rotation and zooming, to ensure robust recognition of CXR images, even in challenging positions. Experimental results demonstrate that the combination of model ensembles and enhanced dataset leads to superior accuracy in diagnosing COVID-19, with an impressive 97.95% accuracy, 98.2% F1 score, and 99.9% AUC-ROC. This approach not only outperforms individual models but also offers a more reliable and efficient solution for COVID-19 detection, particularly in complex cases where symptoms overlap with other respiratory illnesses.

articleTitle: How Corporate Governance Impact to Sustainability Report?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: To achieve the Sustainable Development Goals companies can apply the concept of circular economy to company activities. This concept is to internalize sustainable development in the company's productivity and operational processes in business strategy. Sustainability reports are a form of formal information delivery related to the company's sustainable development activities to the public and stakeholders, so that sustainability reports play an important role in assessing the company's economic, social and environmental performance. The achievement of the company's susitanability performance cannot be separated from the role of corporate governance. This study aims to examine the role of corporate governance in the dimensions of Board Expertise, Board Gender Diversity and Audit Committee Meetings on Sustainability Report in Indonesia. The test was conducted on 109 samples of companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange with a total of 327 observations for the 2019-2021 observation period. Panel data analysis is performed with Eviews 12. The results showed that Board Expertise and Audit Committee Meetings have a positive influence on the Sustainability Report. Meanwhile, the Gender Diversity Board has no effect on the Sustainability Report. This is due to the low participation of female board of directors in companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange due to the small number of women who sit on the company's board of directors.

articleTitle: A Two-Step Feature Selection Procedure to Handle High-Dimensional Data in Regression Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: A wide range of fields are interested in high-dimensional data, including finance, tomography, genetics, etc. Feature selection facilitates the handling of this type of data in Machine Learning. This improves prediction performance by separating relevant variables from irrelevant ones. In this paper, we propose a two-step feature selection method for regression. An initial feature space is reduced by feature screening. To remove extra noise and irrelevant variables, the resulting reduced dataset is fitted to an elastic net model. The proposed method improves elastic net models' prediction results. This is demonstrated in this paper through simulations and real datasets. We demonstrate our method's application to gene co-expression data analysis using the Eyedata dataset.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for Dial a Ride Problem with Time Windows, Case: Hemodialysis Patients Transportation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: End stage renal disease (ESRD) has become a very common disease nowadays as the number of patients is increasing. As a result, an increase in the number of dialysis treatment is noticed. Many dialysis patients treated at dialysis facilities require six trips each week, three trips to dialysis centers and three trips from the dialysis centers. This comes to more than 300 trips each year per patient. This paper focuses on the transportation of patients undergoing the hemodialysis, as they request rides to their treatments. The transportation problem for hemodialysis patients comes with challenges such as the scheduling problems, extra care and support for the patients and the increased cost of the trips. This paper focuses only on reducingthe total cost of transportation. We consider the hemodialysis patients' transportation problem as the problem of determining an optimal routing for a fleet of vehicles used to cover the regular trips requested. The rides must respect some real-life constraints such as the maximum vehicle capacity, availabilityof the vehicle, patient's schedule … etc. The study focuses on the dial a ride problem with a time window (DARPTW), which is a type of Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) that is known in the literature as a complex combinatorial optimization problem related to transportation. Mainly used for transporting individuals with requests. In which a set of users must be picked up from an originlocation and they must be delivered to a destination location. The problem is modeled mathematically as a static dial a ride problem (DARP) where the aim or the objectif function is to minimize the total cost of the transportation.

articleTitle: Assessment and Analysis of Occupational Diseases and Accidents in Chlef Glassworks (NOVER)-Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Occupational hazards claim the lives of over 2.3 million individuals annually, and work-related accidents surpass 300 million, according to the International Labor Organization (ILO). Many of these incidents could have been prevented, underscoring the need for a systematic and integrated approach to workplace health and safety. ISO 45001:2018 offers numerous advantages upon implementation, with particular emphasis on improved productivity, reduced costs stemming from downtime and production losses, as well as decreased expenses associated with insurance and lost work days. This study aims to assess the state of occupational health and safety (OHS) in Algeria, highlighting effective mechanisms for preventing work accidents and occupational diseases, regardless of industry or company size. A survey involving open-ended questions was conducted, with participation from workers across the selected company, the new Chlef glassworks (NOVER), a subsidiary of the National Glass and Abrasives Company (ENAVA). The findings and recommendations presented in this study contribute to the enhancement of occupational safety practices within the organization.

articleTitle: On a Rational-Target Model for the Development of Integrated Security System at the Enterprises of the Russia's Oil and Gas Sector
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The article presents analysis of existing approaches to ensuring integrated security at industrial enterprises. This research is focused on the use of an interdisciplinary approach in its provision at enterprises of the oil and gas sector (OGS) of Russia. In the article, the author presents a methodology developed for Russian oil and gas enterprises as the comparative model and flexible approach in the form of an existing and developing integrated security system to reduce various types of damage. The purpose of the study is to solve the scientific problem of developing an integrated security system at the enterprises of the Russian OGS. The presented results of the study prove the feasibility of using the results of assessing the state of integrated security for the enterprises. Thus, an important problem is solved in terms of rationally-targeted allocation of resources that can be used to eliminate violations of precisely those measures that have high rates of impact on reducing damage from accidents and fires. The monitoring results are presented as use of a new rational-target model for the development of oil and gas companies of Russia. This model allows in practice to solve the problem of reducing damage from accidents and fires in the integrated safety system of these enterprises.

articleTitle: Multi-Item Capacitated Lot-Sizing Problem with Parallel Resources, Setups, Backorders and Overtime Decisions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper we study the production planning problem, more precisely we address a lot sizing problem with parallel resources, setup times and costs and backorder costs. The aim of this work is to propose a mathematical operational planning model based on two work organization approaches: the first configuration in regular mode, the second configuration by using overtime with regular hours when demands are high. The developed models have been tested on a production unit in the textile domain industry. The results obtained have made it possible to draw up a work plan that is optimal in terms of cost and time for all the planning periods while ensuring demand satisfaction.

articleTitle: Exploring Vision Transformers for Automated Glaucoma Disease Diagnosis in Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Glaucoma, a challenging disease that can cause irreversible blindness if not detected early, has garnered significant interest in utilizing deep learning and medical imaging for automated diagnosis and categorization. This paper introduces a novel approach for automatic glaucoma detection by leveraging the advancements of Vision Transformers (ViT), which have shown excellent performance in computer vision tasks following their success in natural language processing. Although Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely acknowledged as one of the best techniques for this task, they still face certain challenges. Therefore, extensive hyper-parameter optimizations are performed during the training phase to determine the optimal settings for each ViT model. Subsequently, a comparison is made between the results obtained from two top-performing CNN models. The study employs transfer learning on five retinal fundus image datasets. Experimental results conducted on the combined datasets demonstrate that the proposed ViT-based model is an effective tool for glaucoma detection, achieving an average accuracy of 92.67% using ViT-L32.

articleTitle: IoT Device Connectivity Selection Using a Hybrid Multi-Criteria Group Decision-Making Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems hold immense promise for transforming various aspects of our lives and industries, driving significant societal and economic advancements. This research paper aims to investigate the significance of IoT systems in various domains, focusing specifically on the industrial application, emphasizing the pivotal role of reliable and efficient device connectivity within such systems. To address the challenges posed by uncertainty and ambiguity in real-life scenarios, we proposed the integration of rough set theory with multi-criteria decision-making approaches to evaluate and classify IoT devices in the industrial domain. The utilization of the proposed hybrid multi-criteria group decision-making approach allows us to effectively model and handle the uncertainty arising from expert assessments. This paper emphasized the computation of parameter weights using a chosen weighting technique to facilitate decision-making processes influenced by subjective information. Finally, an example case shows how the framework may be applied.

articleTitle: Portfolio Optimization for Indian Mutual Funds: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper studies the various types of Portfolio optimization techniques. It explains the models and how they differ from each other. The main focus is creating an optimum portfolio of mutual funds with the help of the Mean-Variance, Markowitz Model, Risk Parity and Hierarchical Risk Parity. The portfolios of Mutual funds created by each technique are compared based on expected return, volatility and Sharpe ratio. We also applied a new method, which is a combination of Hierarchical Risk Parity and Mean-Variance, two top performers in the area. The proposed method achieved the best return and an overall robust portfolio.

articleTitle: Two-Machine Flow Shop with Transportation Time and Raw Material Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a two-machine flow shop scheduling problem that takes into account transportation times and resource constraints. The problem involves scheduling a set of jobs on two machines in a flow shop configuration while considering the time required to transport jobs between the machines and the availability of additional resources, such as raw materials, that are essential for job processing. To tackle this problem, we propose a comprehensive approach that incorporates transportation times and resource constraints into the scheduling model. We explicitly consider the time required for job transportation between the two machines, accounting for the realistic dynamics of the production process. Additionally, we address the availability of raw materials, to ensure that the scheduling decisions are feasible. To solve the problem, we develop a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) formulation that captures the transportation times, resource constraints, and scheduling objective. The MILP model aims to minimize the makespan while satisfying the constraints.

articleTitle: Integrated Planning for a Hybrid Manufacturing-Remanufacturing System: a Multi-Objective/Fuzzy-Satisfying Combined Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The present study addresses the issue of joint planning for a hybrid manufacturing-remanufacturing system. The latter includes a single, capacitated machine, which tends to fail randomly. When breakdowns occur, corrective maintenance is performed. Additionally, imperfect preventive maintenance is scheduled to reduce the risk of a failure rate. New products can be manufactured and returned products can be remanufactured in the system under consideration. Remanufacturing is thought to be more eco-friendly because it produces fewer carbon emissions. The objective is to develop an integrated plan that reduces overall economic costs and carbon emissions while increasing system availability. A multi-objective model is proposed and then solved by the weighted sum method. A fuzzy satisfying method is applied to evaluate the best trade-off solution among the Pareto optimal solutions. Extensive computational experiments are carried out to investigate the effects of carbon footprints generated from new and remanufactured products on integrated planning. Results show that remanufacturing helps reduce the need for new products, leading to significant resource savings and less waste.

articleTitle: A Lossless Virtual Reality Based Alternative to Eye-Tracking for Attention Quantification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Precise measurement of visual attention is crucial for various fields such as psychology, neuroscience, and human-computer interaction. Recent scientific literature has focused on eye-tracking techniques to quantify visual allocation or to predict it. Eye tracking is certainly an efficient and accurate technique, but it comes with a high cost and a limited context of use. In this paper, we propose a novel computational model that accurately quantifies attention allocation in a virtual reality setting. The experimental results demonstrate that our model performs seamlessly with minimum hardware requirements. Our findings suggest that this model has the potential to measure spatio-visual attention allocation accurately and reliably over extended periods, and could be a serious alternative to eye-tracking techniques in a variety of usage, such as therapy interventions.

articleTitle: Automatic generation of a process shutdown system fault tree using a computer program KB3 (Sonatrach-FCP)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Automated dependability analysis has become a necessity due to the scale and complexity of modern systems. In this context, this paper is devoted to using a computer program called KB3 for probabilistic modeling of an operational process shutdown system's behavior, which ensures consistency, saves time, and is even easily accessible to non-specialists. Based on a graphical description of the structure and elementary characteristics of the system under study, using a generic knowledge base written in the Figaro language, the model developed automatically constructs the associated fault tree, which is then used quantitatively to obtain the probability of dangerous failure of the entire process shutdown system and its various constituent sub-barriers. This paper analyzes the performance of a process shutdown system using KB3 software, which is crucial for preserving operational well installations' safety. Initially using the reliability block diagram (RBD) knowledge base, the modeling process ensures a simple and flexible representation of the barrier system, including common causes of failure using the binomial failure rate model. The process produces a fault tree, which is time-consuming to build manually. Quantifying this fault tree gives the average probability of failure on demand (PFDavg) of the entire system and its components, which is essential for estimating the frequencies of occurrence of scenarios. However, to assess the impact of disregarding the existing standby relationship, the system is also modeled using the Boolean logic-driven Markov process (BDMP) knowledge base, showing no significant difference in numerical results.

articleTitle: Healthcare Decision-Making with an ECG-Based Biometric System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Biometric systems that provide accurate identification are essential for making informed decisions in various fields. In this study, we propose a novel approach for identifying medical patients using the QRS waveform of their ECG signal. ECG signals are a highly secure biometric trait as they are difficult to spoof and reproduce. To derive a representative QRS waveform, the signals were subject to preprocessing via a 4th-order bandpass filter, amplitude normalization, and R-peak detection through the Pan-Tompkins algorithm. Subsequently, a vector encompassing 50 samples before and after each index was generated. An identification accuracy of 99.47% was achieved using 48 healthy subjects from the PTB Diagnostic ECG Database. To further test the system, we used 282 healthy and diseased subjects from the same database and achieved an accuracy of 97.60%. Our proposed approach provides a promising solution for biometric identification, which can improve decision-making in various fields such as security and healthcare. With the increasing demand for accurate identification, our study highlights the potential for ECG-based biometrics as a secure and reliable modality for decision-making.

articleTitle: Enhancing Decision-Making in Ranking Multiple Energy Sources: A Linguistic-Based Multi-Criteria Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Energy plays a vital role in sustaining human life and exerting a substantial influence on a nation's economic growth. Assessing diverse energy sources is critical for fostering socio-environmental development and facilitating techno-economic progress. These sources can be classified as renewable (biomass, hydroelectric, solar, wind, and geothermal) or nonrenewable (coal, natural gas, and oil). However, the challenge lies in effectively evaluating and selecting the most suitable energy sources, considering complex linguistic information and multiple criteria. In this study, we propose a linguistic MCGDM approach to assess and rank energy sources in Tunisia. This method effectively handles decision makers' diverse linguistic information. The first phase involves determining criteria weights using the AHP method based on expert opinions in the energy field. Then, the 2-Tuple WASPAS method is applied to evaluate various energy sources. The results provide a ranking of energy policies in Tunisia, from the best to the worst.

articleTitle: Impact of Industrial Risks on the Environment and Simulation by PHAST Software *CASE: HP Separator – DR HBK – SONATRACH
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Explosion hazards can pose a serious threat to the environment. Unexpected blasts can have serious consequences on terrestrial, marine and atmospheric ecosystems. These risks can arise from various sources, such as industrial installations, transport of hazardous materials, accidental explosions or terrorist activities. In this paper, we will explore the harmful effects of explosions on the environment and the importance of taking preventive measures to protect our fragile ecosystem. Our work consists of a risk analysis to determine exactly the impact of industrial risks on people and the environment. The study focuses on the HP separator at DR HBK (Haoud Berkaoui) SONATRACH. We applied the HAZOP (Hazard and operability study) method as well as the X-RISK software, then a simulation of our results by PHAST software (Process Hazard Analysis Software Tool).

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Scoring Approach for Moody's Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Asbtract: The rating agencies play a strongly emphasized role in the world economy thanks to their credit ratings. They have called into question after the American subprime crisis of 2008 and also the European sovereign debt crisis. These agencies hide their analytical methods, which put this subject in ambiguity. In this study, we are interested in sovereign rating, more specifically in the rating of countries by the rating agency Moody's which is based on four factors. We propose in particular to use the fuzzy sets theory to model the imprecision related to scoring scales of Moody's methodology. The developed approach is then applied to a diversified sample of 15 countries with different ratings. Based on a comparison between the found results and the ratings provided by Moody's, we conclude that the degree of compatibility between the two methods is important but it exists some differences.

articleTitle: Centrifugal Compressor Maintenance Using Fault Tree and a Bayesian Network Methods for System Reliability Analysis and Dependability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Oil and gas refining units are considered among the important establishments in the economy of countries, as they depend on them for the production and export of energy. These units base their work on rotating machines such as gas turbines (GT), gearboxes (GB) and centrifugal compressors (CC), the CC is considered the basic pillar of the unit, it is also the first responsible of the unit shutdown at times, as its damage leads to great economic losses such as a decrease in oil and gas production, and this is what makes it a focus and concern for the producing countries. Therefore, maintaining the safety of centrifugal compressors increases the reliability of the system and the continuity of the unit's work permanently and continuously, and this can only be achieved with good monitoring and continuous maintenance, and with all this care from the manufacturers and the preventive measures used, they may be exposed to some defects and risks that cause damage to the internal parts such as bearings, shaft, … etc. Therefore, to raise the reliability and extend the life cycle of compressors, we must mainly rely on continuous inspection and accurate diagnosis to reduce various defects. In this paper, we studied two different cases of two compressors, one of which was subjected to vibrations and the other to high temperatures in the bearings at AL-MERK and BRN units in in southern Algeria. where the unit was completely stopped to fix this defect, this made us think about how to know the main causes of this malfunction. Where we adopted in this paper a hybrid approach, which is a methodology that evaluates the reliability of the system by combining two methods, one traditional is the Fault Tree (FT) to identify events and find out the type of defects that cause the main failure, and the second is a Bayesian Network (BN) relies on artificial intelligence to know the impact of each event on the system, This study helps in analyzing the system reliability, and predicting all the causes that would impede the continuity of the compressors work. Through pre-stored data collected by maintenance experts and monitoring workers, relying on a Bayesian network to identify the fragile components in the system and the most influential ones and calculate the extent of their impact on the system. Finally, by performing this analysis, we found that vibration is the main cause of compressor failure.

articleTitle: Does the Quality of Real Economic Growth Occur in Indonesia? Pro-Poor Based on Human Capital Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to investigate whether the quality of real economic growth occurs in Indonesia which is pro-poor based on human capital. The data used in this study is panel data sourced from the Indonesian Central Bureau of Statistics. The panel data covers 505 regencies/cities spread across 33 provinces in Indonesia during 2014-2020. The total number of panel data is 3535 in 7 years. The panel data model is used to attain the purpose of this study. The results of this study show that the economic growth of the 505 regencies/cities in Indonesia during 2014-2020 has not been pro-poor economic growth yet or the economic growth has not improved the economic conditions of the poor. This highlights that the quality of economic growth in Indonesia is still low. Therefore, the Indonesian government has to formulate a new economic framework orientation that is more focused on labor-intensive which is based on human capital through reforming pro-poor education and health programs and public infrastructures (Aggregate Supply Side). In addition, the quality of fiscal and monetary policy management (Aggregate Demand Side) which is pro-poor has to be strengthened. This comprehensive policy will shape the long-term self-sufficient quality of economic growth.

articleTitle: A Study on the Resiliency of Coffee Roaster Business in Northern Thailand Region
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Today's coffee shop and coffee roastery businesses are more mushrooming from the past. The coffee supply chain in Thailand, especially in the northern region, produces the most Arabica coffee in the country. In the last few years, the demand and coffee consumption volume has been higher than the output, and any disruption at any stage can directly impact the firm. This paper aims to prioritize the significant factors by using the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (Fuzzy AHP) method based on the supply chain resilience concept under two dimensions, vulnerable and respond capacity, characteristic of supply chain resilience. This article will help researchers to understand the resilience concepts by prioritizing factors that influenced the coffee roastery and any related field under the supply chain resilience concept to prepare and resist possible disruption and unpredicted events.

articleTitle: Do Zakat and Price Stability Matter for Poverty Reduction in Indonesia?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study explores the contribution of zakat and price stability to poverty reduction in Indonesia from January 2011 to June 2021. Specifically, this study empirically explores the short-term and long-term relationships between zakat, gold prices, exchange rates, oil prices, and poverty in Indonesia. Using the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM), this study recorded that zakat and gold price stability contribute to short- and long-term poverty reduction. On the other hand, the stability of exchange rates and oil prices have reduced poverty in the long-term. These findings suggest the Indonesian government's importance in enhancing zakat management by implementing good zakat governance principles and ensuring prices of gold, oil, and exchange rate stability through proper macroeconomic policies to alleviate poverty.

articleTitle: Resolution Approach for Cardinality Constrained Portfolio Selection Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Cardinality-constrained portfolio selection is one of the most practical models explored to solve hard-real world limited problems encountered by investors in the stock market. A new resolution approach is suggested in this work using a procedure of selection to choose the portfolio components, followed by a local search meta-heuristic to determine the proportions of investment in selected assets.

articleTitle: Robust and Intelligent Control for PV System of Two Converters:DC-DC Converter/ Single-Phase Modular Multilevel Converter to Operate Grid Connected
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper proposed a Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) incorporating a Sliding Mode Controller (SMC) technique to control the output current of MMC and the Fuzzy Logic (FL) controller maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is used to extract maximum power from the PV array. In photovoltaic systems: the DC-DC Boost converter is usually employed in the adaptation stage between the PV panel and the DC-AC converters on the other hand, it is used for boosting the array voltage and achieving maximum power point tracking for the PV array to the DC-link and a modular multilevel converter that serves as an interface. An MMCs main control objective is to synchronize the grid voltage and current while controlling the DC link voltage. Designing a sliding mode controller of output current for an injected pure sinusoidal current is the main goal of this paper. In previous literature output current strategy was based on a proportional resonant controller (PR); but currently, became advised Robust and Intelligent Controller. For example, in this work, in order to provide a high dynamic performance of MMC and power quality injected into the grid, we build a Sliding Mode Controller-based technique. Then, by using MATLAB/Simulink, the effectiveness and viability of the suggested method are demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Algorithm Development for Solving a Flexible Job Shop Problem (FJSP)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Scheduling has been a prominent area of research for decades, involving the expression, classification, and resolution of various scheduling problems. Many of these problems are computationally challenging, demanding sophisticated algorithms for effective solutions. In this paper, we present a study of the scheduling problem on machines with downtime, with the primary objective of reducing the makespan. We propose a flexible job shop scheduling system equipped with six machines capable of producing six types of parts. To evaluate this system, we utilize modeling and simulation techniques within LEKIN and ARENA software. In the subsequent sections, we introduce our novel algorithm to address machine unavailability and optimize the scheduling process. By comparing the results obtained through simulation experiments, we assess the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm and its impact on the makespan reduction.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Global Central Bank Digital Currencies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The current study aims to describe and analyse the digital currencies issued by 11 countries across six continents.
