The paper also aims to create a base for the initiation of a digital currency. With cryptocurrency posing certain threats, Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) may emerge as a safe alternative. The Atlantic Council report states that nearly one hundred countries in the world are exploring the possibility of introducing CBDCs and at the same time, 11 countries have fully launched CBDCs. In this context, the present study takes a comparative approach, and focuses on the need and rationale for CBDCs as stated by different countries, their implementation mechanisms, current status, adoption rate, initiatives taken to create awareness among citizens, and emerging lessons. The study is descriptive in nature and is based on secondary data drawn from publications by the Central Banks of the countries, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank, the Atlantic Council CBDC tracker, Research Papers and newspapers /online websites, etc.

articleTitle: The Influence of Intellectual Capital, Profitability, and Good Corporate Governance on Financial Performance in Manufacturing Companies Listed on IDX (2016-2020)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the relationship between intellectual capital, profitability, and good corporate governance. This study examined manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2016 and 2020 to test the hypotheses. Multiple Linear Regression is the data analysis method used in this quantitative study. The population consisted of manufacturing companies that were listed on IDX, and the 245 observed samples were collected using the purposive sampling method. The secondary data was obtained from the 2016–2020 annual reports of manufacturing companies listed on the IDX. The results showed that financial performance was positively and significantly impacted by intellectual capital, profitability, and good corporate governance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Optical Fiber Bragg Grating's Performance for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This article presents the design, simulation, and analysis of an optical fiber Bragg grating (OFBG) sensor for use in medical applications. The paper focuses on optimizing the grating period values by using particular interrogation wavelengths. The principle of detection of this sensor is based on the change in the period of the grating which is caused by the application of a strain. The impacts of an FBG's opto-geometric are examined through simulations using coupled mode theory in the Grating Mod module of the Rsoft Photonics CAD program. The findings show that the Bragg wavelength shifts and changes in value in response to period modifications, demonstrating a high level of FBG sensitivity. By considering a wide range of influential factors, these sensors have the potential to accurately forecast their performance and provide reliable measurements in complex biomedical settings. Additionally, the FBG's reflecting properties are modified to provide sensitive sensors that can operate in real-life conditions. This type of sensor of 1mm size has the capability to forecast its performance in intricate biomedical settings, taking into consideration influential factors such as electromagnetic interference, humidity, temperature fluctuations, and other essential environmental elements.

articleTitle: Mathematical Formulation of the Permutation Flow-Shop Scheduling Problem Considering Transport Activity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we extend the well-known Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling Problem (PFSP) by integrating a flood of identical Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) for the transport of semi-finished jobs between machines. The objective of this study is to mathematically formulate the problem of minimizing the maximum completion time. This parameter is known as the makespan. A Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is therefore proposed to model formally the PFSP with AGVs. This model can be used to solve small instances. To validate the proposed mathematical model as well as for solving the large instances of the problem we have adapted the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) metaheuristic.

articleTitle: HMC-COVID-19: Hidden Markov Chains Model for COVID-19 Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Markov chains are probabilistic models that are useful in different image processing tasks. This paper presents an approach based on Hidden Markov Chain (HMCs) to diagnose COVID-19, that we named HMC-COVID-19. To assess the performance of the proposed solution, we use a public dataset of chest X-RAY images. Our solution has been evaluated using the accuracy of prediction. The preliminary results are promising and can be further enhanced.

articleTitle: A Trained Fuzzy Expert System to Detect Emergent Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The concept of emergence has gained attention due to its relevance in understanding complex systems, its cross-disciplinary nature, advancements in computational tools, challenges to reductionism, its connections to artificial intelligence and machine learning, philosophical implications, and potential real-world applications. As our understanding of emergent phenomena grows, it continues to shape our perspective on how the world works at various scales. In this article, we propose a novel method for detecting emerging behavior in a multi-agent system based on a fuzzy expert system. In addition, The article explores how interactions can be used as a metric to identify emergent behaviors in the Boids model and outlines the initial effects of a three-step process: (1) Representation and acquisition of simulation data,(2) Building a fuzzy expert system,(3)Learning process and emergence detection. Since this is a part of ongoing research, future direction is also discussed.

articleTitle: Contribution of Unsupervised Clustering Algorithms to Patient Safety Culture Promotion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Patient safety culture (PSC) is a linked to improved organizational performances and fewer adverse events in healthcare. Mainly, PSC is assessed using self-administered questionnaires that define PSC through a number of dimensions. Nevertheless, the latter suffers from a major limit that is dimensional scores aggregation to obtain PSC overall level. To overcome this constraint, the proposed approach consists of applying unsupervised clustering algorithms (i.e. K-means & HAC) to group HEs sharing similar PSC profiles. This approach was applied on PSC assessment data in 10 Algerian pubic HEs. Results showed that HEs can be grouped into 3 clusters having different PSC profiles. The proposed approach has the merit of guiding decision makers to propose adapted improvement actions based on shared inter and intra cluster problematic PSC dimensions.

articleTitle: Application of the FRAM Method to an Oil Production System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Oil production systems are prone to accidents with tragic consequences. Therefore, many studies have focused on preventing these accidents by identifying the main risk factors in these systems. Among these factors, we find failures in the operation of production systems. In this article, our goal is to focus on oil production systems and to highlight the importance of optimal performance of their functions. Thus, it is essential to carry out a thorough evaluation in order to identify the critical functions that have a significant impact on their proper functioning. This evaluation requires the use of appropriate methods to analyze the functions of oil production systems. In the context of this study, we favor the use of the Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM), which proves to be very effective for evaluating the interaction of functions in general and for defining the dynamic links between these different functions.

articleTitle: Semantic-Layer: A High-Level Semantic Ontology For Data-Driven Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Recent years have seen a breakthrough in object detection in computer vision thanks to the development of deep learning algorithms. Although neural approaches appear to perform on par with or even better than human judgment for several benchmarks, issues remain for identifying random concepts in random fields. In this paper, we propose and construct a high-level semantic ontology called the “semantic-layer”, which can be used as an inference engine as well as in training for data-driven models, such as, computer vision, image retrieval, and NLP (Natural language processing) systems. In addition, the proposed layer is also destined to query generation systems, which aim to modify or enhance the users' queries before being transmitted to the server of the research engines.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Decision-Making RASS-RATSI Approaches to Rank Soils Olive Tree Growing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In semi-arid areas, agriculture is based on limited and fragile “water and soil” resources that are often overexploited. To ensure the sustainability of agricultural land management in rural areas, environmental assessment must be integrated to support both policy-makers and local stakeholders in their decision-making. Sustainable intensification in agriculture entails the need for management practices able to boost the activity of soil biogeochemical cycles, functional to long-lasting soil biological fertility. This work aims to propose a tool that can evaluate the different soils for olive culture. In this study, two MCDM approaches, RASS (ranking alternatives based on surface similarity) and RATSI (ranking alternatives based on surface trace index), were presented to rank soils for olive tree growing in Tunisian orchards.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of the Evolution of Roughness Parameter During Friction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Surface roughness allows to characterize the surface state and the degradation of materials subjected to different tribological mechanisms, hence the quantification of this important parameter, which influences the behavior of friction, wear and even adhesion coatings in wet or dry environment, is essential. Thereby, the aim of this study is to evaluate the evolution of peaks density “Spd” one of roughness parameters, in a mechanical contact and the effect of the friction parameters namely the load “Py”, the sliding speed “V” and the distance traveled “D” on this parameter. Friction tests were carried out according to the experimental methodology of complete plans 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> on a steel surface X52 using a tribometer type Ball-Pin/Disc against ball 100C6. The roughness parameters were measured using a 3D laser source profilometer Cyber Technologies SCAN CT100. The results indicate that the applied load is the most relevant parameter that influences the peaks density. This parameter negatively affects the “Spd”. Whereas, the sliding speed and distance “D” had a slight; and positive influence on the “Spd”. The processing of the results a leads to a mathematical model highlighting the peaks density “Spd” as a function of “Py”, “V” and “D” as well as their interactions.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptive Healthcare Platforms Development: A Dynamic Product Line Approach Driven by Ontologies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Software reuse has been a fundamental and recurring problem in software engineering since its inception. Its main objective is to reduce software development and maintenance costs by facilitating the reuse of existing software components. Currently, the approach of software product lines and software architecture enables the simultaneous achievement of these objectives. The objectives include the development of a Healthcare dynamic product line and the identification of reusable components. This dynamic product line will later allow the generation of various applications based on user requirements. Additionally, we aim to construct a domain ontology that represents the feature model of e-health, determining the common functionalities and variabilities of software in this domain. The architecture is modeled following component-based principles to enhance reuse. In summary, our research project aims to address the challenges of software reuse by developing an e-health product line, constructing a domain ontology, and adopting a component oriented architecture.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Skin Lesion Classification Based on Dermoscopic Images and Meta-Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Skin cancer is one of the most dangerous diseases, it can be deadly if not treated at an early stage. The intervention of deep learning has made a significant contribution in the field of dermatology medicine. In this work, we applied deep learning methods represented by Two dimensional Convolutional Neural Network and Multi-layer Perceptron on uni-modal and multi-modal data while taking into consideration two classes (malignant and benign). Additionally, due to the imbalanced data-set, we transformed images into a vector to solve this problem by applying SMOTE method, which is very important in classification problems.

articleTitle: An Investigation on the Use of Heterogeneous Ensemble Machine Learning in Predicting Two Measures of Software Maintainability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The software maintainability is considered as an indispensable factor to acclaim the quality of a particular software. This attribute indicates the amount of work required to correct or modify software. The prediction of the maintainability of software systems makes it possible to give an answer in terms of effort for software developers. To date, many works in the literature have used several machine learning techniques to predict the maintainability. The maintainability is often measured via the change metric which calculates the number of lines changed per class in an object oriented system. In this paper, we focus our investigation on the use of heterogeneous ensemble learning techniques (Stacking and Voting) for the prediction of two maintainability metrics: the change and the maintainability index. We propose a model that combines the predictions of three individual models that we have chosen in order to improve the accuracy calculated via Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Magnitude of Relative Error (MMRE). Our study has shown that Stacking is the best model to use to predict maintainability.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization for Sustainable Manufacturing-Remanufacturing System with Maintenance Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study focuses on sustainable parallel manufacturing/remanufacturing lines that incorporate maintenance strategies, within a multi-objective context. Each line is a single machine prone to random breakdowns. When a machine fails, only minimal repairs are performed; however, imperfect maintenance is planned to help control the risk of failure rates. The purpose of our work focuses on determining the optimal integrated manufacturing, remanufacturing, and maintenance plans that minimize both the total economic cost and the energy consumed by both processes. We develop a multi-objective mathematical model and implement an enhanced version of the I-constraint method to solve it. Moreover, the most efficient solution within the Pareto set is found through TOPSIS, the Technique of Order Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution. A series of numerical experiments are then conducted to investigate the influence of manufacturing, remanufacturing, and maintenance integration on system sustainability. The Pareto front was accurately generated by AUGMECON2, which included efficient solutions that are not located at the corners.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Static and Rotary Electrostatic Separators for Plastic Waste Sorting using DEM Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The electrostatic separation technique, in which charged particles are sorted using a high-intensity electric field, is ideal for the treatment of plastic granular waste. Since analyzing the influence of some factors experimentally is complex and time-consuming, numerical methods such as the discrete element method are employed to appropriately adjust these variables, control the trajectory of particles and adequately comprehend the process in detail. This work focused on the development of a model capable of predicting particle motion within a static inclined plane separator and a novel rotary conical separator, along comparing the outcomes between both systems. Particle charge and high voltage were chosen as the main factors to evaluate separation efficiency, with a cohesive effect included, which is frequently overlooked in research. The added value of the rotational arrangement which drastically reduced particle agglomeration commonly encountered in industrial equipment was highlighted.

articleTitle: Multi-Step Prediction of PM2.5 Concentration Using a Sequence-to-Sequence Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of a sequence-to-sequence approach for multi-step prediction of PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentrations. The aim is to analyze the effects of varying the lengths of input and output sequences, as well as the use of different architectures, specifically LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) and Transformer. The models were trained using three years of PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentration data. The results indicate that the LSTM models, incorporating time series decomposition, achieved the highest performances. The LSTM models outperformed the transformer with multi-head attention architecture, consistent with previous studies that concluded that transformers did not exhibit superior performance for multi-step time series prediction. These findings suggest that LSTM models, with the inclusion of time series decomposition, are valuable for predicting multi-step PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> concentrations in urban areas grappling with air pollution challenges.

articleTitle: Offensive Language Detection in Code-Mixed Bambara-French Corpus: Evaluating machine learning and deep learning classifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we deal with offensive and abusive language detection on Bambara language, which is an under-resourced language mainly spoken in Mali and some other African countries. As a first work on this language, we aim to release OBAM v1.0 corpus compiling 4k of texts that are labeled as normal, offensive and abusive. In addition, we have carried out a set of experiments with different configurations using various machine learning and deep learning classifiers. In overall, the classifiers produced acceptable results (0.80 and 0.73 of F-score in two-category and three-category classification, respectively), but they could be improved by expanding the corpus and proposing new features.

articleTitle: Applying Decision Aid Science to Support Customer Choices for Web Services Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The growing popularity of Web services has been accompanied by a significant increase in the number of Web services operations. For a given need: Several Web services operations may exist. The customer is satisfied. He has many choices, but at the same time, he feels lost: what is the best choice to make? In this work, we try to support the client's decision. We are not trying to decide in its place but to justify his choices. We seek to rank the list of returned operations (Web services operations) from the best to the least good according to customer preferences using Multiple-criteria decision analysis, more precisely the PROMETHEE II method.

articleTitle: Decoding e-WOM: Unravelling Its Role in Driving Purchase Intentions on E-commerce Websites
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: E-WOM is a prominent source of information about online products on various e-commerce sites, significantly affecting decision-making. This study tried to explore purchase intention, especially in the context of the product type, and to know whether there is any generation difference in sharing reviews online. This study uses primary data collected through a questionnaire from frequent buyers of products from online platforms. Data was collected from 135 respondents through convenience sampling. From the research outcomes, it is found that there is maximum review sharing for electronic products in the product types considered for this study. The study also highlighted no generation difference in the review sharing.

articleTitle: Developing the Antecedents of Perceived Barriers to Aid Decision-Making for Safeguarding the Sustainability of Intangible Heritage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The preservation of intangible heritage (IH) followed by the advancement of culture is not only a goal in itself, but it also directly contributes to many other United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDGs), such as promoting resilient and sustainable cities, supporting economic growth, creating employment opportunities, and even reducing gender disparity. This exploratory study is an attempt to bridge the gap in our understanding of the barriers to safeguarding and sustaining intangible heritage specifically from the standpoint of architects and facilitate decision-making. Based on an extensive review of literature and discussions with domain experts the following five constructs were identified which could be described as perceived barriers towards IH: Role Complexity, Non-Physical Qualities, Unclear Domain Relationships, Uncertain Definition, and Participatory Problems. The relationships between the five barriers and IH were tested through confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) followed by structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypothesized model based on a dataset of survey responses received from 198 architects in India.

articleTitle: The Lot Sizing Problem with Return and Profit Maximisation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: We address the lot sizing problem without capacity with return and price. The goal is to maximize profit and minimize total costs while meeting customer demands that include new product demands and used product demands The problem addressed in this work is one of the lot sizing problems with remanufacturing found in the literature and our addition is to introduce the purchase price of returns as a decision variable. The problem of lot sizing with return has received a lot of attention from many scientists due to the importance of the subject in manufacturing systems In particular, studies on remanufacturing, refurbishment and prices Simultaneous, which is very rare in literature. In this study, we include three processes: refurbishment, disassembly and remanufacturing of parts, and assembly of new products. The process feeds on the requirements of second-hand (refurbished) and New products. we propose a mathematical model for this problem, and We conducted numerical tests to examine the impact of corresponding decisions on the overall profit in various scenarios. the results show that the integration of the purchase price of returns as a decision variable, refurbishing process can lead to a significant profit gain.

articleTitle: Ressource Planning and Scheduling for Operating Room Management: Current State and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Operating theatre management is one of the most critical activities in the hospital environment, with a major financial impact due to its high consumption of human and material resources. In this paper, we provide a literature review of recent research dealing with integrated operating room planning and scheduling. We focus on several key points that are considered as a means of classifying recent studies in this field, such as resource constraints, solution methods and objective functions. These points form the outline of our classification of the existing literature. Our objective is to systematically review the research literature concerning operating room assignment and sequencing problems. Perspectives that need to be addressed in the future are identified for further investigation.

articleTitle: Real Time Fire and Smoke Detection Techniques Using Improved Transfer Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Classical fire and smoke detection systems cannot be used outdoors and do not guarantee the necessary availability for real-time applications. The objective of this research paper is to use a deep neural network to detect fire and smoke in outdoor environments using an embedded system with a camera. Recently, after significant progress in programming structures and, above all, in the field of machine learning, embedded systems are now able to perform real-time edge computing. This work proposes improved transfer learning approaches to perform computer vision fire and smoke detection using a convolutional neural network (CNN). Three transfer learning models (VGG-16, VGG-19, and YOLOv5) have been enhanced and used in order to detect once fire or smoke appears in any camera, then the system can detect them and immediately send an alert to the corresponding supervisors. The performances of the proposed algorithms are verified on a common database; then on real scenarios.

articleTitle: Vowels' Articulatory Location Classification based on Formant Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Modelling vowels is a crucial step in many applications such as speech understanding, human age analysis, accents differentiation, security and E-learning. This paper proposes building a statistical model for the US English vowels based on formant frequencies, which are extracted from real speech samples. Vowels are classified according to their articulatory-acoustic characteristics into front and back vowels. Three different approaches have been tested in this research, the K-means clustering, Fisher's linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and non-linear Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The proposed GMM model is used to classify vowels with the help of the Expectation Maximization (EM) algorithm. The results show that K-means analysis did not produce a convenient classification of vowel formants. Meanwhile, the automatic perception is highly achievable when formant data are projected on different coordinates using Fisher's LDA (FLDA). The classification error in the FLDA is close to that of the quadratic discriminant function of the EM algorithm. Although EM algorithm that was based on GMM gave better classification when it was tested, Fisher's LDA gave nearly the same results with significantly less computations.

articleTitle: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Efficient Pre-Processing and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Early diagnosis of the brain condition known as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) could significantly reduce the high healthcare costs typically involved with treating ASD. Autism's fiscal toll emphasizes the importance of developing easy and effective detection instruments. Therefore, a quick ASD evaluation is essential to helping healthcare professionals and letting people know if they should seek a formal clinical diagnosis. Currently, there are very few autism datasets related to screening accessible, most of which are based on genetics. To expose critical information about autism screening, this work suggests applying a novel machine learning framework that contains vital characteristics and performing predictive analysis utilising a Support vector machine, logistic regression, K-nearest neighbour, and random forest. The main objective of this study is to develop a system for the early detection of children at risk for autism spectrum disorders (ASD).

articleTitle: Gaussian Processes for Efficient Photovoltaic Power Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems play a pivotal role in the transition towards sustainable energy sources. Grid operators rely on dependable forecasts to balance supply and demand dynamics, ensure grid stability, and optimize energy dispatch strategies. Accurate prediction of PV power enables effective integration of solar energy into the electrical grid. Grid operators need reliable forecasts to balance supply and demand, manage grid stability, and optimize energy dispatch. This study explores the use of Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models for accurate PV power prediction, specifically comparing GPR with four different kernel functions: Rational Quadratic (QR), Squared Exponential (SE), Matern 5/2 (M52), and Exponential (Exp). Real-world data from a grid-connected PV system in Algeria is employed for evaluation. Results demonstrate that the GPR with SE kernel outperforms the other kernels, exhibiting the highest prediction accuracy based on statistical scores such as root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: Open Innovation System Theory Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This paper aims to explain the open innovation (OI) process using systems theory, showing (a) pathways towards their further development and (b) explaining evolutionary developments. We introduce a meta-view of the two disciplinary poles, i open innovation and ii evolutionary system, system order principles, and system stability. We apply then ii to i or OI using eight explaining Axioms. Finally, we give examples of how to use this axiomatic method in an innovation process and a practical OI method.

articleTitle: Blockchain Adoption for a Sustainable Agricultural Supply Chain: Opportunities and Challenges for the Dairy Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Blockchain is a decentralized and tamper-resistant digital ledger technology that records and stores transactions or information in a secure and transparent manner across a network of computers. Each transaction, or “block,” is linked to the previous one, creating a continuous chain of information. This technology ensures data integrity, transparency, and trust among participants, as changes to the blockchain require consensus from the network, making it highly resistant to manipulation or unauthorized alterations. It is a technology that has the potential to dramatically transform the supply chains. This study investigates the opportunities and challenges of blockchain technology in transforming supply chains, and the legitimacy of its implementation into the dairy industry. By conducting a comprehensive review of recent literature at the intersection of blockchain, sustainable supply chain, and the dairy supply chain, this paper aims to determine the best blockchain-based solution for improving the efficiency and sustainability of dairy supply chains.

articleTitle: A Robust-Facial Expressions Recognition System using Deep Learning Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In recent times, Facial Expression Recognition strategies are viewed as the main field of examination in biometric innovation. In this exploration paper, we present a Facial Expression Recognition (FER) framework partitioned into three stages: The Viola-Jones face detection algorithm, facial image enhancement utilizing Adaptive Histogram Equalization calculation (AHE), and component learning for classification. For learning the highlights followed by classification we utilized VGG16, ResNet50 Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) models for the proposed framework. Our trial work was performed on the JAFEE data set and CK+ information base. At last, the correlation with different strategies on the two data sets shows the heartiness and adequacy of the proposed approach. The ResNet50 architecture achieved high accuracy rates of 98.21% and 97.08<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for the respective evaluations.

articleTitle: Significant Feature Dimensionality Reduction for Histopathology Image Retrieval as a Tool for Healthcare Decisions Support
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Content-Based Histopathology Image Retrieval (CBHIR) is often used as a powerful tool to support decision making by clinicians, and facilitate the disease detection and diagnosis. In CBHIR, feature extraction plays a key role for representing and interpreting histopathological images of several tissues. To enhance the retrieval performance, combining several features is commonly used in CBHIR; however, the high-dimension of the combined features often makes the process of retrieving very time-consuming. To resolve this challenge, we propose in this paper a method for reducing the dimension of a combined feature vector formed of several features extracted using the Improved local binary patterns (ILBP) descriptor, and coded in different color spaces. To reduce the size of the combined color ILBP feature, we adopt a selection scheme for picking only the most important patterns of the latter according to optimal weights associated to the patterns. The optimal weights are generated using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The results of the experiments performed on Kimia Path960 dataset confirm the efficiency of the proposed method in reducing the feature dimensionality and the retrieval time while maintaining as good as or better retrieval performance than the combined feature.

articleTitle: How Important is Workload Affect Occupational Frustration? A Bibliometrics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study presents a bibliometrics analysis and scientific mapping of research on workload and occupational frustration within the field of organizational behavior from 2001 to 2023. Data from the Scopus database were analyzed using VOSviewer software. The study explores publication trends, identifies the most productive authors, countries, and publication sources, and analyzes keyword co-occurrence. Findings reveal increasing publication fluctuations, with the highest number of publications in 2022 (111 documents). Spector P.E emerges as the most productive author with 21 articles, and Fox S (2001) as the most cited author with 779 citations. The United States is the most productive country with 36 articles and 8,891 citations. The Journal of Occupational Health Psychology is the most productive publication source with 13 articles, while the Journal of Vocational Behavior leads in citation count with 1,815 citations. Keyword analysis highlights stress, workload, and job satisfaction as frequently mentioned keywords. This study contributes to the understanding of workload and occupational frustration in organizational behavior. It emphasizes the need for further research, particularly in Indonesia where the topic remains underexplored compared to international studies, enabling organizations to develop effective interventions, optimize workload distribution, and enhance employee well-being. Future scholars, particularly in Indonesia, are encouraged to contribute to the literature in this field.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in the Medical Field: A Comprehensive Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Machine learning utilization in medicine has increased interest over the last few years. With its impressive results in treating diseases and medical conditions, it will be important to understand and analyze how the scientific community has used it. Thus, opening up space for new research and opportunities in medicine. The objective of this study is to review the literature on machine learning applications in the medical sector. Therefore, we conducted an extensive research by reviewing recent studies and surveys on machine-learning health solutions. As a result, we offer, in this paper, a fresh study affirming the foundations and necessities of a machine learning application in the medical field. We also provide a breakdown of current research trends, which highlights future research opportunities.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Intelligent Prediction System Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The mortality rate from Lung Cancer is high, and the disease is notoriously difficult to treat. It was the third most frequent mortality reason for women and the leading cause of male mortality, according to data compiled by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) Cancer Research Facility. Additionally, they provided rates of cancer occurrence and mortality for a total of 36 different cancers occurring in 185 different countries. Typically, early tumor detection is essential for effective therapy. Early cancers can be efficiently examined to help patients recover quickly. Traditional medical imaging techniques, such as X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, etc., offer little promise for lung tumor identification. CNNs are capable of exact image processing. This paper provides a probabilistic deep 2D CNN diagnosis method for lung cancer (CNNs). This algorithm is considered the best in image classification, which gives better results, making the proposed system more efficient. The accuracy values obtained are 86%, the recall of 92%, and the F1-score is 87%.

articleTitle: Exploring Forecasting and Prediction Processes for Decision-Making to Promote the Photovoltaic Energy Integration into the Grid: A Mini Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: As solar energy is increasingly integrated into the electricity grid, the power system faces several technical challenges posed by the fluctuating renewable source. This paper reviews the forecast and prediction processes, which are crucial components for Grid-Connected PV power plants. According to the literature, photovoltaic predictions can be made for various time scales, ranging from very short-term forecasts to short-term, medium-term, and long-term projections. The temporal resolution depends on the specific needs and applications of the prediction, such as optimizing energy management or planning for grid integration. The spatial resolution corresponds to the sampling area of the prediction. The accuracy of a photovoltaic (PV) forecast can be measured by comparing the predicted values with the actual observed values. Several performance parameters provide quantitative measures to aid in evaluating the efficacy of the forecasting model, such as RMSE, r2, MAE, and MAPE. Drawing on existing literature, the scientific community experiences various forecast techniques, which are classified mainly into persistence methods, physical techniques, statistical techniques, and hybrid models, with a prevailing trend toward hybrid deep-learning models in last years. However, certain gaps exist, particularly related to complexity and time consumption. With increasing PV penetrations, the impact of incorrect forecasts in the grid can be larger. In some electricity markets, solar producers can face penalties when deviations between forecast and produced energy exceed a tolerance band. Numerous companies actively participate in the field of PV forecasting. Among them are Schneider Electric, Enphase Energy, SteadySun, and GreenPowerMonitor.

articleTitle: The Importance of Assets and Liabilities in Sustainability Disclosure: Evidence from Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The shift in the way businesses operate has transitioned from solely focusing on generating profits to adopting a more sustainable development-oriented approach. Companies that embrace sustainable business practices with the intention of achieving long-term viability now communicate their efforts through disclosures about their sustainability initiatives. This research focuses on examining how the presentation of assets and liabilities impacts the disclosure of sustainability initiatives. The investigation involved studying a selection of 200 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange that have issued sustainability reports. The study encompassed a substantial time span, from 2013 to 2021, and employed panel data analysis using EViews software. The outcomes of the panel data analysis revealed that the size of a company's assets does indeed influence the extent of sustainability disclosure. However, when scrutinizing the results based on industry-specific sensitivities, it was evident that the impact differed significantly. Notably, the effect of asset size on sustainability disclosure was more pronounced in companies with lower profiles compared to those with higher profiles. Contrarily, the assessment of the influence of liabilities on sustainability disclosure displayed no significant impact overall. Nevertheless, upon segmenting the liability results according to industry-specific dynamics, a discernible effect emerged. Specifically, the impact of liabilities on sustainability disclosure was more conspicuous in companies with lower profiles, as opposed to those with higher profiles. In light of the study's findings, certain recommendations can be made. Firstly, it is apparent that current policies promoting sustainability disclosures predominantly rely on administrative penalties, which have not proven fully effective in motivating companies to openly share their sustainability endeavors. As a result, the study suggests that in the future, there is a need for more binding and stringent policies and penalties to be established by both governmental bodies and the financial market to encourage and enforce enhanced sustainability disclosures.

articleTitle: Budget Governance Evidence In Indonesian Selected Universities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to identify the factors that influence budget governance in Indonesian universities. The research was conducted at 79 universities, and the participants included members of the academic community at various levels, including departments, programs, faculties, and the university as a whole. Confirmatory analysis was utilized to examine the factors proposed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), which are predictable, aligned, coherent, transparent and accessible, participation, accountability, budget execution, value for money, sustainability, and integrity. The findings reveal that all the examined indicators are significant; however, some inconsistencies were observed in predictable, participation, value for money, transparent and accessible, accountability, and integrity dimensions. This indicates that budget governance in Indonesian universities has not been fully achieved, and further improvements are required to enhance budgeting practices and overall governance effectiveness.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Power of Feature Selection: Enhancing Data Analysis Through Effective Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The practical implications of these findings lie in their ability to extract features that benefit coaches, analysts, and stakeholders in optimizing team strategies and predicting match outcomes. While recognizing limitations, such as the reliance on a specific dataset from the Qatar FIFA World Cup 2022 league matches and the exclusion of contextual elements, it is crucial to acknowledge the need for future research to validate and expand upon these findings. This can be achieved by incorporating diverse datasets and considering additional contextual factors during the feature selection process for data analysis. The real-world implications of these studies can be found in their capacity to extract traits that help coaches, analysts, and stakeholders optimize team plans and anticipate match outcomes. While noting limitations such as the use of a single dataset from the Qatar FIFA World Cup 2022 league matches and the removal of contextual components, it is vital to recognise the need for additional research to validate and expand on these findings. This is possible by integrating several datasets and taking additional contextual elements into account during the feature selection process for data analysis.

articleTitle: Optimized Fog Colony Framework for Efficient Service Placement using Hybrid Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The transition from Cloud Computing to Fog Computing is being investigated as the preferred method for rapid data processing in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Fog computing is a decentralized computing paradigm, harnesses the computational capabilities of IoT devices at the network edge to perform data processing and provide real-time services. However, effective service placement in fog environments remains a challenge. This research paper focuses on the lack of efficient techniques for organizing fog devices into optimal fog colonies that possess self-rule capabilities and require minimal energy for administration. We propose a hierarchical clustering-based fog colony architecture to fill this void, which will allow for in-depth investigation and analysis of various colony configurations. The resulting dendrogram includes all feasible colony configurations, and a genetic algorithm is used for precise colony selection based on fitness and accuracy. The multi-objective hybrid genetic algorithm NSGA-II is used to assess how efficiently the suggested framework performs under a variety of conditions. The goal is to reduce the delay between an app's initial interaction with a user and the initial practice of the app. The results show improvements in reaching predefined goals when the proposed strategy is applied to different contexts.

articleTitle: Assessing ANN Architectures for Wind Turbine Power Prediction: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: With the increasing importance of renewable energy sources, wind power has emerged as a significant contributor to the global energy mix. Accurate prediction of wind power production is essential for efficient grid integration and optimal utilization of wind resources. This study presents an investigation into the performance of various artificial neural network (ANN) models for wind power prediction. Different ANN architectures, including narrow, medium, and wide networks, as well as bilayered and trilayered structures, were explored to understand their impact on predictive capabilities. The data used for evaluation was collected from a 2.05 MW Senvion MM82 wind turbine. The performance of the ANN models was compared with Linear Regression (LR), Interactions LR, Robust LR, and Stepwise LR methods. Results revealed that the bilayered and trilayered ANN s achieved the best performance in wind power prediction. This study highlights the potential of ANN models in accurately predicting wind power, thereby facilitating efficient and reliable wind farm operations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Fake Image Detection in Generative Adversarial Networks and Variational Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The rise of deep fake technology has led to growing concerns about its potential misuse for propaganda, disinformation, and even cybercrimes. Deep fake detection has thus become a crucial research area to prevent the spread of fake content and protect digital authenticity. This research investigates the detection of fake human face images using deep learning models. The study utilizes a combination of the CelebA-HQ and FFHQ datasets to create real image labels. Two generative models, a Style-based generator and a Variational Autoencoder, are trained to generate GAN-fake and VAE-fake images, respectively. The deep learning models are then trained and evaluated using both real and fake images. The research focuses on two scenarios: binary net and multi-class net. In the binary net scenario, ResNet50 achieves the highest accuracy of 99.34%, along with excellent precision, recall, and F1-score. VGG16 and VGG19 also perform well in distinguishing between fake and real images. In the multi-class net scenario, ResNet50 again achieves the highest accuracy of 95.25% and balanced F1-score. VGG16 and VGG19 maintain competitive performance, while other models show slightly lower accuracy. These results provide insights into the effectiveness of different deep learning models for detecting fake human face images. ResNet50 consistently performs well in both scenarios, while VGG16 and VGG19 offer reliable alternatives.

articleTitle: A Decision Model for the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Fostering DEI in the Workplace
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming every industry because of its incredible advantages. This study demonstrates how AI technologies are becoming more widely used in the workplace and the enormous opportunities it presents for promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI). However, it also poses risks and difficulties that should be carefully assessed. For this study, primary data is collected using the structured interview process. 80 respondents were selected comprising managers from companies with more than 100 employees that have adopted AI in fostering DEI. This research paper presents a decision model for organizations to adopt AI effectively in a manner that supports DEI goals. The study has been conducted in the context of the Indian companies. The author has proposed a model which outlines key considerations, ethical principles, and implementation strategies, providing a comprehensive framework to guide decision-making processes. By integrating AI technology with DEI initiatives, organizations can leverage the potential of AI while minimizing bias, promoting fairness, and enhancing inclusivity in the workplace.

articleTitle: Using Multicriteria Analysis to Compromise on a Battery Storage Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: In our research, we employ the multicriteria decision-making (MCD) method, which incorporates Euclidean distance, the creation of ideal and anti-ideal profiles, and the weighting of criteria to express preferences. This approach makes it easier to make well-informed choices among several, frequently competing alternatives. Our goal is to choose the best storage battery among four different varieties, including AGM lead-acid, GEL lead-acid, lithium, and nickel, taking into account aspects like cost, performance, and depth of discharge. We may objectively compare the benefits and drawbacks of each kind of battery by using the well-known TOPSIS approach. Instead of pursuing an ideal solution, which may be elusive, our strategy tries to help decision-makers reach an agreeable compromise. Our research helps to improve the integration of renewable energy sources into storage systems, where storage batteries are essential in stabilising intermittent solar and wind energy production.

articleTitle: Philippine Rice Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: As with many Asian countries, rice is a principal food in the Philippines providing nearly half of the daily caloric needs of Filipinos. Rice plants are susceptible to many diseases whose spread is induced by weather conditions such as high humidity and rainfall producing detrimental effects on crop's yield and thus affecting the country's food security. Rapid, early, and correct detection of rice plant disease is warranted to prevent spread and avoiding its detrimental effects through an early institution of preventive measures. The purpose of the study is to ascertain the distinguishing capability of convolutional neural networks in the recognition of rice plant disease. Deep learning models (base convolutional neural and pre-trained networks) were applied to the Philippine Rice Disease Dataset to diagnose rice plant diseases. VGG16 obtained the best performance with a 96% accuracy, 99% sensitivity, 97% precision, 98% F1-score, and a 0.834 normalized Matthews Correlation Coefficient. InceptionV3 also generated superior performance while the base model had a lower diagnostic capability. These models can be useful complementary tools which may be deployed as quick and non-invasive diagnostic support instruments assisting farmers in the evaluation of rice diseases especially in communities where agricultural experts are limited. Farmers would gain more valid outcomes with these technological approaches, enabling them to institute cost-effective measures. Thus, effective management of rice plant diseases, optimized and efficient use of available resources leading to improved rice crop productivity can be achieved. A working partnership of agriculturists and machine learning enthusiasts is crucial to achieve the desired goal of early identification of rice plant diseases for prompt intervention efforts to be instituted.

articleTitle: Exploring the Dynamics of Team Formation in Human-Artificial Intelligence Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The emergence of collaborative human-artificial intelligence is a promising approach for improving team performance. This study intends to analyze the models of team formation and draw the lines for human and artificial intelligence collaboration. By investigating the existing models of the stages of human-human team development, the study highlights the characteristics of team development stages and explores the prospect of having human-artificial intelligence teams instead throughout the stages to ensure better humanartificial intelligence communication and team cohesion. Considering the unique nature of human-artificial intelligence interaction, the study identifies a number of characteristics that are applicable to the scenario of team development when teams consisting of humans and artificial intelligence are employed.

articleTitle: Distributed Machine Learning for Predicting Customer Behavior While Preserving Privacy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Analyzing customer behavior has great value, that's why researchers until this day are trying to more understand customer behavior, because this enables them to realize what's behind purchase intention, how and what customers want to buy, and what are the factors that affect customer behavior. Big data, artificial intelligence, and machine learning are the three most critical pillars on which the concept of business analytics is based, which leads to ideal customer behavior analyzes and through which customer behavior can be predicted. The benefits of predicting customer behavior are many, such as increasing sales and profits, maintaining existing customers and attracting more. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to analyze the existing methods for predicting customer behavior in addition to identifying the types of federated learning and the suitable type for each scenario. This study provides a comprehensive description of customer behavior prediction techniques. The authors found that there are many models used to predict customer behavior and that there are four main factors affecting customer behavior. The most prominent approaches to maintain data privacy are differential privacy and homomorphic encryption. Moreover, there are three main types of federated learning which are horizontal, vertical and transfer federated learning. As a future study, one of the federated learning approaches will be used to predict customer behavior.

articleTitle: Unveiling City's Branding Strategy as the Premier Islamic and Tsunami Tourism Destination: The Case of Banda Aceh, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study examines the branding strategy of Banda Aceh, Indonesia, as the premier Islamic and tsunami tourism destination. Banda Aceh has gained international recognition for its rich Islamic heritage and its profound connection to the devastating tsunami of 2004. The research aims to unveil the city's branding strategy and explore the relationship between the Islamic-related object (IRO) variable and the Tsunami tourism destination (TTD) through quantitative analysis. Of 29.213 tourists who visited the city in 2019, 200 of them were selected as the sample of the study using a simple random sampling technique. The primary data collected through questionnaires and interviews were then analyzed using multiple regression techniques. Based on the results of data analysis using multiple regression techniques, this study found that Islamic-related objects and Tsunami-related objects play an important role in determining Tsunami tourism destination in the city of Banda Aceh. These findings are supported by the robustness tests conducted, which confirmed the validity of the proposed model and its suitability for policy inference. This highlights the importance of preserving and promoting the city's Islamic heritage and incorporating tsunami-related elements in the branding strategy. Policy makers should allocate resources and develop policies to support these efforts, collaborating with local communities and cultural organizations for effective integration. Additionally, they should prioritize the development of cultural and educational experiences, involve local communities, and implement educational programs to raise awareness of cultural preservation and responsible tourism practices.

articleTitle: A Reliable Neural Network Approach for Monitoring and Diagnosing Bearing Faults in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to develop a comprehensive approach for monitoring and diagnosing faults in induction motors, with a specific focus on bearing faults, which are the most prevalent type of fault in these motors. A monitoring system based on artificial intelligence techniques and a multilayer perceptron neural network is utilized to predict these faults. The artificial network is trained using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, optimizing its performance as a diag nostic tool for induction machines. Temporal vibration indicators obtained from vibration analysis serve as inputs to the network, enabling the identification of fault presence or absence. The obtained results demonstrate the significant influence of training and test parameters and data on the neural network's performance. This research provides valuable insights into the application of artificial neural networks in fault diagnosis for induction motors, offering a reliable approach for proactive maintenance and enhancing the overall reliability of industrial motor systems.

articleTitle: Distributed Dynamics Scheduling Based Reinforcement Learning: Importance and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: When it comes to scheduling choices inside complex industrial systems, the dynamic job shop scheduling problem (DJSSP) poses substantial difficulties. Deep learning, artificial intelligence (AI), and reinforcement learning approaches have all shown promising solutions in recent years to enhance the effectiveness and performance of DJSSP systems. This study provides a detailed analysis of the DJSSP literature, with an emphasis on these cutting-edge methods. The review adopts a rational methodology that includes an exhaustive search of many databases from 1995 to 2023. Articles were chosen based on predetermined qualifying criteria, taking into account their applicability to the DJSSP and the methodology used. This paper also examines how software design affects research, how industry influences research, and the types of research outputs that are disclosed. The findings provide valuable insights into the current state of research and offer guidance for future advancements in optimizing dynamic job-shop scheduling using advanced learning techniques.

articleTitle: Green Finance and Climate Change Nexus in Indonesia: Autoregressive Distributed Lag Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between green financing and Indonesia's climate change, specifically the short- and long-term directions of influence. The time period under investigation covered monthly data from 2018, the year that Indonesia's first green sukuk was issued, to 2022. The study is enhanced by estimation using Granger causality and autoregressive distributed lag. The results show that while green stock and sukuk have a negative impact on climate change over the long term, lag-1 and lag-2 are significantly impacted negatively in the short term by green sukuk. In the short run, green stocks are beneficial. While the industrial production index has a negative short-term impact on climate change, it has a favorable long-term impact. This suggests that there has to be an increase in both the short- and long-term tenors of Indonesia's global green sukuk.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Waste Management Systems in Algeria and Other Countries : a literature review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Waste management is a crucial issue for developing countries, as it affects their environment, health and economy. Poor waste management can lead to pollution, disease outbreaks, greenhouse gas emissions and social conflicts. Therefore, developing countries need to adopt strategic decisions to improve their waste management systems and practices. This article explores waste management in some developed country such as Singapore, Sweden, Germany, and Japan and compare them with Algerian situation. The objective is to assess the gap between the approaches adopted by these countries, in order to identify good practices and opportunities for improvement in Algeria. The document examines the scientific research and academic contribution in the field of waste management, then presents the types of waste. It analyzes the infrastructures, the technologies used, the methods of collection, sorting, recycling, and disposal of waste. Relevant policies, departments and agencies in each country are also reviewed, with an emphasis on laws and regulations specific to waste management. The results of this comparative study highlight the strengths and weaknesses of the waste management system in Algeria compared to other countries. Good practices identified elsewhere are discussed, highlighting opportunities for knowledge transfer and best practices that can be applied in Algeria. Finally, recommendations are made to improve the waste management system in Algeria, taking into account the socioeconomic and environmental realities of the country.

articleTitle: Green Blockchain and Smart Homes: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Over the last few decades, one of the biggest challenges facing technology, especially the Internet of Things (IoT), has been system vulnerability, centralization, the inefficient ways of storing and transforming data, making these systems vulnerable to fraud, hacking and other forms of manipulation. Additionally, they often charged high fees and long processing times. The advent of blockchain solves many problems through the use of specific techniques and efficiency interventions such as decentralization manner without the help of any third party, high security, consensus deals, anonymity and others. On the other hand, there are also disadvantages. In this context, many research has focused on the use of green blockchain (GBC) to improve performance and mitigate the problems and significant impacts of traditional blockchain and therefore create a positive green think minding. In this paper, we query the Scopus database with keywords to retrieve relevant publications to explore the rationale behind the need for sustainable development and the actual green blockchain technology being used in smart homes.

articleTitle: Techniques and Methods for Anomalies Detection in ECG as a Support for Medical Decision in Healthcare: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Latest scientific evidence for healthcare decisions are applied by doctors and patients jointly through decision support tools. As it is already known, anomaly detection in time series is an important data mining task for discovering unusual patterns in time series data. For instance, in the medical domain, early and precise detection of types of heart arrhythmia is important to help in making decision, detect heart disease and choose an appropriate treatment using the electrocardiogram (ECG) as a tool. The present work aims to provide a review of tools and methods in detection anomalies. The study shows that, globally speaking, the main approaches for that purpose are ECG signal processing tools, statistical and mathematical tools, pattern recognition tools and artificial intelligence algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Traffic Management Using Internet of Vehicles: A Layered Architecture-Based System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The number of vehicles on the planet is growing rapidly, and cities are expected to continue growing. This leads to an increase in the number of road automobiles as well as traffic congestion, air pollution, and inevitable accidents, which can affect the societal side, the economy, and the environment. These issues explain why many research programs around the world aim to improve transportation systems; this is indeed a difficult task because the distributed, open, dynamic, and partially controllable nature of transport networks makes it a complex area. In this paper, we provide a concise review of the impact of integrating the Internet of Vehicles in intelligent transportation systems. Furthermore, we propose a layered architecture-based IoV to efficiently manage and monitor urban traffic systems. Overall, the proposed architecture aims to improve coordination and communication among the road network entities, leading to improved transportation systems.

articleTitle: Tapping into the Popularity of Social Media Stars: A Management Model for Influencer Marketing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Individuals with a huge following, referred to as influencers, have acquired enormous popularity and recognition as a result of the growth of social media channels. In this highly competitive digital landscape, influencer marketing provides a distinctive edge as influencers have the power to shape buyer perceptions through their posts and recommendations. The present study aims to explore the potential advantages that motivate marketers to adopt influencer marketing over other conventional marketing strategies. In addition, this study intends to identify the popular influencer marketing strategies that drive the success of influencer marketing approaches. Brands must meticulously identify influencers who share their core beliefs, consumer base, and promotional goals, as social media trends are continuously changing. This study adopts an exploratory approach by conducting semi-structured interviews with 27 marketing managers of Indian organisations that have deployed influencer marketing for their promotional campaigns. These marketing managers were selected for the study by using a judgemental sampling technique as it was crucial that these managers possess the required knowledge and expertise pertaining to the adoption of influencer marketing by organisations. When deciding on influencers to collaborate with, comprehensive scrutiny and proper careful planning are required. Therefore, based on the findings, the authors propose an influencer marketing decision model that will enable marketers to select an appropriate influencer for their influencer marketing initiatives and ensure its successful implementation.

articleTitle: Critical Success Factors for Humanitarian Logistics: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Humanitarian logistics (HL) is vital in disaster response and emergency relief operations. Understanding the critical success factors (CSFs) enables humanitarian organizations to optimize their operations and enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of their logistics processes. Through a comprehensive examination of literature between 2005 and 2023, this study identifies crucial elements (CSFs). It classifies them into ‘vital few’ and ‘useful many’ based on their occurrence frequencies using Pareto analysis. The results identify CSFs, including the application of modern information technology, well-planned emergency relief system, coordination, and collaboration with stakeholders, timely and relief need assessment, organizational structure, clear awareness of responsibilities, and materials and resources as vital factors. The analysis highlights the significance of the vital factors in ensuring the timely and effective delivery of aid and services to affected populations. By understanding and addressing these critical success factors, humanitarian organizations can enhance their capacity to respond to crises and positively impact the lives of those in need.

articleTitle: Quantum Optimization in Engineering: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Since its beginning, quantum computing has opened up a plethora of new perspectives and advantages., including its ability to exponentially accelerate computing processes. A large amount of research has been devoted to developing innovative methods for solving a variety of engineering problems by designing quantum versions of numerous mathematical processes. In this paper, we review the state of the art in these new techniques from the standpoint of quantum computer creation and efficiency enhancement, with an emphasis on the most widespread mathematical optimization techniques for engineering applications. It also emphasizes the obstacles and constraints associated with the use of quantum computing, as well as the major prospects for future contributions. This paper is providing a useful resource for engineering researchers who are likely to seek solutions from quantum computing.

articleTitle: Optimizing Resource Allocation in the Flexible Job Shop Problem: Assessing the Impact of Rest Breaks on Task Strenuousness Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The integration of collaborative robots (cobots) in production workshops aims to enhance productivity while minimizing physical strain for human operators. However, physical strain is often treated merely as a constraint rather than as an objective to address. To effectively model the production process and incorporate human factors, it is crucial to employ an appropriate index that accounts for precise ergonomic rules. In this paper, we propose a method to organize induced waiting times in the context of Flexible Job Shop Scheduling (FJSP) with the primary goal of evaluating the effects of rest breaks on fatigue generated by physical efforts in various operations. Our method introduces a specific index, based on ergonomic standards, to assess the difficulty level of operations for both humans and robots. The index incorporates normalized strain values, ensuring its generalizability across diverse industries. Moreover, the method considers a wide range of work scenarios, encompassing both individual and collaborative settings, making it applicable to different industrial contexts. Furthermore, we analyze the accumulated fatigue experienced by human agents over several scenarios, both before and after the optimization process. By doing so, we not only gain insights into the production process but also facilitate the optimization of human-robot collaboration. Our findings indicate the influence of rest break durations on the recovery of human workers and offer strategies to reduce strenuousness during production planning involving cobots. This work contributes to creating a more efficient and ergonomic working environment for all parties involved, promoting human well-being and presence in the industrial workshop. By emphasizing the significance of considering physical strain and rest breaks as essential factors in the 5.0 factory, we pave the way for improved human-robot interaction and performance in manufacturing settings.

articleTitle: A Comparison of the Finest Electrical Energy Forecast Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Predicting today's utilization of energy will determine how powerful it is in the future. Generators can change their output by foreseeing the demand for electricity. As a result, shortages or overproduction are prevented while resource consumption is optimized. These electrical services may be impacted by the season, the weather, volatility, and other occurrences. Therefore, it is essential for service providers to be able to foresee these situations and have a window of opportunity to take preventative action. The forecasting of electricity load could be demonstrated using a time series prediction problem. Many architectures can contribute in this field to build extremely accurate deep learning models for Short-term Load Forecasting (STLF) in electrical networks. In this paper, the used models are Random Forest, Transformer, Convolutional Neural Network, Linear Regression and Decision Trees. The supplier will choose among this models or combine them to realise an effective prediction.

articleTitle: The Impact Of Quantum Computing In Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Genetic algorithms are widely used for solving optimization problems. As the search space of the problem is augmented, the probability of falling into local minima will be augmented as well. Previous works showed that the adjusted phase (i.e. required modification per generation), may enhance badly the optimality reaching. Moreover, the search for suitable probabilities on crossover and mutation results in huge computational complexity. Recent developments in quantum technology have shown that quantum computers can provide a dramatic advantage over classical computers. This paper will be oriented toward computer scientists interested in the quantum genetic algorithm (QGA). Therefore, we will present a discussion, of the pros, and cons of classical GA. We survey the “state of the art” of the most known techniques for evolving evolutionary algorithms and quantum computing. We intend in this work to help researchers and application developers in gaining insights into the power of quantum computing mechanisms. This science can inherently treat the balance between exploration and exploitation of the search space. This property is due to the use of Q-bits. The orientation toward the best solution is due to the use of Q-gates.

articleTitle: Promoting Financial Inclusion Through Financial Literacy, Socialization, and Commitment to the Implementation of Islamic Financial Institutions' Law in Aceh, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Aiming to foster Islamic financial inclusion, this research explores how Islamic financial literacy, socialization, and commitment to adopting the Qanun have affected Islamic financial institutions in Aceh Province, Indonesia. The study's participants are residents from Aceh Province who have used Islamic Financial Institutions services. Using multi-stage random sampling, this study selected a sample of 100 clients from various Islamic Financial Institutions in Aceh Province who were at least 17 years old, and we gathered their responses to questionnaires.
