The partial least squares (PLS) model was used for the data analysis. The findings indicate that improving financial literacy among the Acehnese population positively influences financial inclusion. Enhanced financial literacy equips individuals with better knowledge of Islamic financial products and services, leading to increased adoption and utilization. Awareness and familiarity with Islamic finance are vital to increasing its accessibility and overcoming difficulties, and hence, effective socialization initiatives play a crucial role in doing so. Further, a commitment to Qanun implementation offers a legal foundation for Islamic financial institutions, which in turn encourages the growth of a variety of products and services and helps to expand financial inclusion in the area. Strengthening financial literacy, socialization, and regulatory commitment supports the growth of the Islamic finance sector and contributes to overall welfare improvement. Collaborative efforts among stakeholders are crucial for promoting financial literacy, enhancing socialization, and ensuring robust regulations, ultimately fostering greater Islamic financial inclusion and economic growth in Aceh Province, Indonesia.

articleTitle: Evaluating Account Representative Competence and its Impact on Tax Collection Performance: A Strength Typology-30 Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: This study examines how Account Representatives' tax revenue collection performance is determined by competence, leadership, and co-workers. Measurement is conducted using the Strength Typology-30 categorisation scale to find a personality profile that aligns with Account Representative tasks and functions based on the Regulation of Minister of Finance Number 45/PMK.01/2021. Data collection is done by sending the Strength Typology 30 test link and a Google Form questionnaire to 140 Account Representatives working in the Tax Service Offices within the Regional Office of the Directorate General of Taxes in Aceh as respondents. The data was analyzed using the multiple linear regression analysis method with the IBM SPSS 22 software program. The research findings reveal that competence, leadership, and co-workers play a crucial role in enhancing tax revenue performance by account representatives. There are 128 respondents categorised as “competent” and “sufficiently competent” on the Strength Typology-30 test, indicating that the majority of Account Representatives possess sufficient competence aligned with Account Representative tasks and functions. This study provides an overview of individual Account Representative competence based on the results of the Strength Typology-30 test, which can serve as a reference for the Directorate General of Taxes in devising human resource development policies, especially for the position of Account Representative.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Storm Damage Prediction in Nova Scotia, Canada
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Power loss due to storms is a recurring problem in Nova Scotia (NS) that affects hundreds of thousands of households every year. Accurate prediction of the location and magnitude of power outages caused by storms is crucial for developing effective response plans. This study proposes and tests two machine learning models, a deep neural network and a random forest, for storm damage prediction in NS. Historical weather and damage data are used to train the models, which incorporate multiple input features such as wind speed, gust and direction. Both models are found capable of predicting outages with a mean absolute error of around 0.05 (i.e., an accuracy of 95%), outperforming the currently-used regression based tool. Furthermore, comparison against other machine learning algorithms demonstrates the advantages of the proposed models in terms of accuracy, interpretability, scalability and robustness.

articleTitle: Potatoes Supply Chain Challenges and Opportunities in Algeria : A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: The Agri-Food Supply Chain (AFSC) has become a focal point of attention in recent times due to the intersection of technology and integrated Supply Chain (SC) performance. Current research endeavors aim to minimize waste, maximize yield, and enhance planning while ensuring chain traceability and maintaining product price equilibrium. This paper offers a comprehensive summary of the latest and most prominent in the AFSC optimization studies that address the emerging challenges in the potatoes SC and the role of technological advancements. The research is categorized based on the planning horizon, followed by an exploration of cutting-edge decision-support technologies relevant to the potato SC. Over the past decade, technological advancements and data analysis have provided significant advantages in developing and implementing integrated AFSC strategies. The paper analyzes various research contributions to propose future design and planning solutions tailored to the Algerian potato AFSC. Furthermore, it includes references to optimization models developed in Algeria and recent reports pertaining to this sector, with a focus on policy actions and motivations. Finally, the study delves into a thorough analysis of how the potato AFSC can be developed, considering the constraints posed by the existing market and structure. By amalgamating research findings and insights, this paper aims to guide the development of a more efficient and sustainable potato AFSC in Algeria.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms Investigation for Urban Drainage Decision Systems: Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Applications (DASA)
abstract: Urban drainage systems may derive advantages from the implementation of machine learning methods for decision-making and cleansing operations. Conventional decision support systems are rendered ineffective in tackling the intricate and indeterminate aspects of urban planning concerns. This paper provides an overview of machine learning methods applied in modeling urban drainage systems, which are classified into five distinct approaches: Supervised learning, unsupervised learning, deep learning, Reinforcement learning, and finally hybrid approaches combining two or more previous algorithms. This study explores also diverse datasets that researchers can utilize in their scientific investigations. The present related works exploration reveals that a majority of studies lean towards reinforcement learning and deep learning methods, predominantly utilizing local datasets. Consequently, we have compiled a table containing some reference datasets. These advancements result in enhanced accuracy and efficiency in predicting and managing urban drainage systems.
